a140.speaker: Hakainde Hichilema, President of Zambia
a140.name: Hakainde Hichilema
a140.title: President of Zambia
a140.speech: Has warned that those who have encroached on land reserved for the expansion of Palabana University should be ready to surrender it back to the University before it is forcibly reclaimed from them and given back to the rightful owners.

a213.speaker: Reserve Bank of Malawi, Monthly Economic Review (report)
a213.name: Reserve Bank of Malawi
a213.title: Monthly Economic Review (report)
a213.speech: Detailed that the national budget deficit surged to K300 billion in May 2025; links the deterioration to a sharp decline in revenue collections coupled with rising recurrent expenditure. Total government revenue for May fell by K86.7 billion (19.9 percent) to K348.4 billion, largely due to a K54.8 billion (17.4 percent) drop in tax collections, which stood at K260.7 billion; grant inflows decreased by K8.3 billion (12.4 percent) to K58.2 billion; total spending rose by K82.8 billion (14.6 percent) to K648.4 billion, with recurrent expenditure jumping by K94 billion (21.2 percent) to K536.3 billion while development spending was cut by K11.2 billion (9.1 percent) to K112.1 billion.

a213.speaker: Oxfam International
a213.name: Oxfam International
a213.speech: Recently listed Malawi among 44 African countries that have cut back on social spending in order to meet debt obligations, despite already being classified as in debt distress; the report attributes rising inequality on the continent to elite-friendly fiscal systems, limited wealth taxation, and intensifying pressure on public services.

a213.speaker: Agnes Nyirongo, economic governance officer at the Centre for Social Concern
a213.name: Agnes Nyirongo
a213.title: economic governance officer at the Centre for Social Concern
a213.speech: Said the reduction in development expenditure threatens to derail long-term poverty reduction efforts: "The cuts to development spending are especially worrying. They undermine long-term poverty reduction. If we continue increasing recurrent costs—largely salaries and administrative overheads—while cutting investments in health, education and infrastructure, we're simply locking ourselves into a low-growth, high-inequality future."

a213.speaker: Alick Nyasulu, economic statistician
a213.name: Alick Nyasulu
a213.title: economic statistician
a213.speech: In an earlier interview, cautioned that rising government deficits, coupled with the foreign aid and debt squeeze, will force the government to borrow more from the domestic market; warned that this would worsen the crowding out effect—a situation where the private sector cannot access loans from commercial banks. He said in a WhatsApp response: "Interest rates will continue to rise because government can afford to pay more, but the private sector cannot grow under such expensive financing conditions."

a213.speaker: Malawi government, Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs
a213.name: Malawi government
a213.title: Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs
a213.speech: Projected that the government will close the 2025/26 financial year with a budget deficit of K2.47 trillion that will be primarily financed through domestic borrowing amounting to K2.33 trillion and foreign borrowing of K145.78 billion.

a343.speaker: Oromia Cooperative Bank (announcement)
a343.name: Oromia Cooperative Bank (announcement)
a343.speech: Announced that through the digital loan service it is implementing under the name "Michu" it has provided more than 7.9 billion birr in loans to more than 270,000 borrowers.

a343.speaker: Dirbe Asfaw, Chief Executive Officer of Oromia Cooperative Bank
a343.name: Dirbe Asfaw
a343.title: Chief Executive Officer of Oromia Cooperative Bank
a343.speech: Explained that, in line with the plan the bank set out to expand the accessibility of credit, it has in a short time enabled many borrowers to benefit through Michu ; indicated that such an arrangement has not only made a loan service that used to reach only a few available to the many, but has also helped create a convenient alternative for micro and small enterprises that had difficulty obtaining banking services ; recalling that, as was recently heard from the National Bank of Ethiopia, no more than 350,000 borrowers had been using the loans the country's banks were providing, noted that the bank's ability to provide loans to more than 270,000 people within two years is a major change ; stated that the change being seen in providing such facilitated loans to small borrowers will be continued in a manner based on borrowers' needs, strengthening a loan service that had been confined to a few so that it can reach all sections of society.

a343.speaker: National Bank of Ethiopia
a343.name: National Bank of Ethiopia
a343.speech: Recently stated that no more than 350,000 borrowers had been using the loans provided by the country's banks.

a343.speaker: Oromia Cooperative Bank (information obtained from the bank)
a343.name: Oromia Cooperative Bank (information obtained from the bank)
a343.speech: Information obtained from the bank explains that borrowers taking loans through the Michu application increasingly work with the money they borrow, make a profit and repay immediately, and that one borrower has been able to borrow repeatedly up to 85 times ; additional information obtained from the bank indicates that although more than 270,000 small borrowers were reached by 30 Meskerem, there is demand from up to 400,000 people to use the loan service ; according to the bank's information the number of regular borrowers does not exceed 35,000.

a343.speaker: Dirbe Asfaw, Chief Executive Officer of Oromia Cooperative Bank
a343.name: Dirbe Asfaw
a343.title: Chief Executive Officer of Oromia Cooperative Bank
a343.speech: Said the bank has so far launched at more than 200 of its branches the service that made it possible to digitise money movements at its smart branches, departing from the traditional paper-based system, and to do so effectively ; said that Oromia Cooperative Bank, which has more than 13 million customers and is the private bank with the largest customer base, is expanding digital banking services in order to serve those customers better, and hinted that there will be new digital banking services it will unveil soon.

a343.speaker: Solomon Desta, Deputy Governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia
a343.name: Solomon Desta
a343.title: Deputy Governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia
a343.speech: For his part, said that Oromia Cooperative Bank has been becoming notable for launching various new digital banking services; recalling that the service launched that day is the first in Ethiopia, the deputy governor said Oromia Cooperative Bank is among the banks achieving progress in the sector ; said that when Oromia Cooperative Bank began operations its capacity was small, so there was a perception of "how will it survive in the market?", but added that it was unexpected that it has now risen from the bottom to become one of the banks the National Bank of Ethiopia classifies as large under its criteria, and gave recognition to the work it is now doing in digital banking.

a602.speaker: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a602.name: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a602.speech: In December 2024, announced Liberia's eligibility for a compact, but the process was paused due to a presidential transition in the United States.

a602.speaker: Augustine Ngafuan, Liberian Finance and Development Planning Minister
a602.name: Augustine Ngafuan
a602.title: Liberian Finance and Development Planning Minister
a602.speech: Addressing a news conference on Monday, July 28, 2025, said, "The MCC Board has informed the government that at its upcoming board meeting Liberia's eligibility may be reaffirmed for a compact." ; "When Liberia's eligibility is reaffirmed by the MCC Board, the government would proceed with setting up the MCC Country Office, recruit the relevant staff, and begin developing the compact."

a602.speaker: Augustine Ngafuan, Liberian Finance and Development Planning Minister
a602.name: Augustine Ngafuan
a602.title: Liberian Finance and Development Planning Minister
a602.speech: Stated that, given President Boakai's recent engagements with the leadership of the MCC in the U.S., he is optimistic that Liberia will be allowed to proceed with the program.

a658.speaker: Experts in international relations
a658.name: Experts in international relations
a658.speech: Believe that an immediate and unconditional cease-fire is necessary, which necessitates the involvement of regional and international actors to put pressure on both warring parties to stop the violence and enter into negotiations.

a658.speaker: African Union (AU) Peace and Security Council (statement)
a658.name: African Union (AU) Peace and Security Council (statement)
a658.speech: Condemned the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) proposal to set up a parallel government in war-torn Sudan and urged the RSF and its affiliated political and social forces to oppose the establishment of a parallel government in the Republic of Sudan, warning that such action would significantly increase the risk of the country's partition ; urged all AU Member States and the international community to refrain from recognising, supporting, or assisting any armed or political group attempting to establish a parallel government or state entity in the Republic of Sudan or its institutions ; "The Council does not recognise the alleged parallel government or entity in the Republic of Sudan." ; reaffirmed its support for the Republic of Sudan's sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity, as well as the peaceful resolution of the current devastating conflict, which has resulted in the world's largest humanitarian crisis, displacing more than 12 million Sudanese civilians ; "The Council urged all parties to heed calls for a ceasefire and unhindered humanitarian access during the holy month of Ramadan, as well as to commit to comprehensive and inclusive peace talks" ; "Council reaffirmed the AU's unwavering commitment to continue collaborating with all Sudanese stakeholders towards finding viable and long-term solutions to permanently silencing the guns in Sudan, based on the AU Roadmap for the Resolution of the Conflict in Sudan, which was adopted by the PSC at the Heads of State and Government level on May 27, 2023" ; endorsed the efforts of the PSC Ad-hoc Presidential Committee and the High-Level Panel on Sudan to find a peaceful political solution to the crisis.

a658.speaker: Government of Sudan (statement)
a658.name: Government of Sudan (statement)
a658.speech: Sudan "welcomes the press statement issued by the African Union Peace and Security Council (PSC) following its meeting this week," which included a clear and unequivocal condemnation of the RSF militia and its affiliates' announcement regarding the establishment of a parallel government, as well as grave concern about this move, warning of the enormous risks it poses to Sudan's unity and the possibility of partition ; "This principled and decisive position from the continental mother organisation emphasises the international community's total rejection of the conspiracy of the genocidal RSF militia and its regional sponsor, as well as those who follow its directives in the region, against Sudan's unity and sovereignty." ; "This has been stated by the United Nations Secretary-General, the United Nations Security Council, the Arab League, the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region, the European Union, and brotherly countries and influential members of the international community." ; "Sudan expresses its gratitude for these clear and consistent positions with international law, which provide strong support to the Sudanese people and their national institutions in defending their sovereignty, unity, dignity, and independence."

a658.speaker: Almoiz Mohamed, media officer at the Sudan Embassy in Nigeria
a658.name: Almoiz Mohamed
a658.title: media officer at the Sudan Embassy in Nigeria
a658.speech: Said the AU statement emphasised Sudan's sovereignty and rejected any separatist attempts that threatened its unity, calling for a firm response to these moves as well as the isolation of any arrangements that threatened the country's sovereignty and integrity ; "We appreciate this responsible stance and commend the courage of member states in making this decision, which strengthens African countries' unity and partnership following the common charters and principles on which African Union is founded."

a658.speaker: Experts (unnamed)
a658.name: Experts (unnamed)
a658.speech: Believe that the longer the conflict lasts, the greater the risk of further instability, regional spillover, and a worsening humanitarian crisis.

a754.speaker: Experts, policy leaders and development partners at the 11th Africa Think Tank Summit
a754.name: Experts
a754.title: policy leaders and development partners at the 11th Africa Think Tank Summit
a754.speech: Urged African governments to adopt fair, transparent and inclusive tax systems built on emerging technologies to reshape the continent's fiscal future and ensure self-reliance.

a754.speaker: Mamadou Biteye, Executive Secretary of the African Capacity Building Foundation (ACBF)
a754.name: Mamadou Biteye
a754.title: Executive Secretary of the African Capacity Building Foundation (ACBF)
a754.speech: In his opening remarks, urged African leaders to move away from donor dependency and focus on transparent and equitable domestic financing, noting that Africa should be ready to fund its own future.

a754.speaker: Zadig Abreha, President of the Africa Leadership Excellence Academy
a754.name: Zadig Abreha
a754.title: President of the Africa Leadership Excellence Academy
a754.speech: "Let us transform taxation from a burden into a badge of honour." ; "Africa must move from being analyzed to becoming the authors of its own progress."

a754.speaker: Aynalem Nigussie, Ethiopia's Minister of Revenue
a754.name: Aynalem Nigussie
a754.title: Ethiopia's Minister of Revenue
a754.speech: Agreed with Abreha and further remarked that policy alone cannot bring about change; rather, it must be matched with the right implementation and cross-sector cooperation.

a754.speaker: Dr. Fekadu Tsega, Policy Studies Institute
a754.name: Dr. Fekadu Tsega
a754.title: Policy Studies Institute
a754.speech: Stressed the need for context-specific and inclusive tax systems that rebuild trust between citizens and the state, noting that "proximity matters between citizens and governance, policy and implementation, Africa and the world."

a754.speaker: Communiqué issued at the end of the 11th Africa Think Tank Summit
a754.name: Communiqué issued at the end of the 11th Africa Think Tank Summit
a754.speech: Urged governments to strengthen domestic resource mobilisation through fair, efficient, and technology-enabled tax systems while reducing reliance on official development assistance and debt; institutionalise evidence-based and transparent PFM systems, including citizen budgets, joint audit follow-up mechanisms, and effective oversight by parliaments and civil society; and leverage AI and digital innovation for predictive revenue analysis, expenditure tracking, and improved compliance across sectors. It also recommended sustainable funding and formal collaboration frameworks to enhance think tanks as key actors, and stated that "participants agreed that ACBF, in partnership with the AUC and AUDA-NEPAD, will disseminate the summit's key recommendations across member states and regional bodies, develop a Post-Summit Action Plan (2025–2026) aligned with the Agenda 2063 Second Ten-Year Implementation Plan, facilitate capacity-building sessions for national PFM actors, and produce an annual Africa PFM Progress Report" ; "ACBF and partners were called upon to scale up capacity-building programmes, leadership development, and the creation of a continental PFM competency framework. Countries were encouraged to explore innovative financing mechanisms such as health and environmental taxes, public-private partnerships, diaspora bonds, and digital economy taxation."

a754.speaker: Mamadou Biteye, Executive Secretary of the African Capacity Building Foundation (ACBF)
a754.name: Mamadou Biteye
a754.title: Executive Secretary of the African Capacity Building Foundation (ACBF)
a754.speech: In his closing remarks, said the summit was able to clearly agree that to bridge the gap between policy and implementation in public financial management requires collaboration through leadership, trust, strong institutions, and the power of African knowledge: "From the rich exchanges on digital taxation and innovative financing to the renewed emphasis on human capital, institutional strengthening, and inclusive participation—one message stands out: Africa is ready to turn knowledge into results. This summit has given us four powerful reminders: Fiscal sovereignty is not optional. If Africa is to fund its schools, hospitals, infrastructure, and climate resilience, it cannot rely indefinitely on external aid." ; "Domestic resource mobilization is not just a budgetary exercise—it is a question of independence and dignity. Implementation is the real frontier. We do not lack policies, roadmaps, or visions. What we lack, too often, is the capacity, the coordination, and sometimes the courage to implement them. This summit has shown that bridging this gap requires political will, institutional reforms, and accountability mechanisms that citizens can trust." ; "Think tanks are not spectators. They are architects, translators, watchdogs, and partners. From designing fiscal models to training civil servants, from monitoring reforms to convening stakeholders, think tanks are central to the journey from taxation to action. Partnership is the only way forward. Governments cannot reform alone. Civil society cannot demand change alone. Development partners cannot finance alone. It is only through collaboration, through co-creation, and through mutual trust that reforms will endure." He also appealed to the participants to ensure that the summit recommendations are translated into policy briefs, action plans, and measurable targets at national, regional, and continental levels that can positively impact the citizenry—farmers, teachers, traders, and youth.

a768.speaker: Sleiman Kwidini, Zimbabwe Health and Child Care deputy Minister
a768.name: Sleiman Kwidini
a768.title: Zimbabwe Health and Child Care deputy Minister
a768.speech: Said this while responding to questions from legislators in the National Assembly on Wednesday, that the government is working to cover the gap created by the withdrawal of donor funding. “Yes, there might indeed be an impact on the withdrawal of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) from World Health Organisation (WHO),” he said. “It is now the mandate of the Ministry and the Government to make sure that these programs which were withdrawn from the Ministry are now wholly owned by the Ministry such that we can cover the gap that has been left by the people who were funding us,” he added ; said issues of HIV and AIDS, malaria and tuberculosis were wholly government programs: “We then had stakeholders who came in to fund those programs. So as we speak right now, our technocrats are making sure that we cover the gap which has been left out by these program implementers because these came in to feed into our policies as a nation. Ministry technocrats are in the process of finding out how best we can come up with possible solutions, especially in budgeting and also human capital which was affected by these funds which have been withdrawn. Basically, the policy is already there and was existing but what has been withdrawn is the support which we were receiving from the funders,” he said.

a768.speaker: US Agency for International Development (USAID, suspension notice)
a768.name: US Agency for International Development (USAID
a768.title: suspension notice)
a768.speech: Effective January 24 this year, the implementing partner was instructed to halt all activities and minimize costs associated with the award during the suspension period.

a811.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a811.name: Marco Rubio
a811.title: US Secretary of State
a811.speech: Said Monday the United States was cancelling 83 per cent of programmes at the US Agency for International Development (USAID). “After a 6-week review, we are officially cancelling 83% of the programmes at USAID,” Rubio said on social media platform X. “The 5,200 contracts that are now cancelled spent tens of billions of dollars in ways that did not serve, (and in some cases even harmed), the core national interests of the United States,” he added ; notably thanked the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), which billionaire Elon Musk is leading in a drive to slash costs and cut jobs across government departments.

a811.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (executive order)
a811.name: Donald Trump
a811.title: US President (executive order)
a811.speech: Signed an executive order in January demanding a freeze on all US foreign aid to give his administration time to assess overseas spending, with an eye to gutting programmes not aligned with his “America First” agenda.

a811.speaker: US State Department
a811.name: US State Department
a811.speech: Had announced on February 26 its intention to cut 92 per cent of the agency’s programme funding, identifying 5,800 grants to be eliminated.

a811.speaker: Trump and his allies
a811.name: Trump and his allies
a811.speech: Have argued that foreign assistance is wasteful and does not serve US interests.

a811.speaker: Aid groups
a811.name: Aid groups
a811.speech: Argue much of the assistance supports US interests by promoting stability and health overseas and warn that cutting aid threatens the lives of vulnerable people.

a1188.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1188.name: Donald Trump
a1188.title: US President
a1188.speech: Stated on Friday that Ukraine had "no cards in hand" in potential negotiations to end the conflict with Russia. "I have had very good discussions with (Russian President Vladimir) Putin, and I have had discussions that were not as good with Ukraine. They have no cards in hand, but they play it hard," he said from the White House, adding: "We are not going to let this continue."

a1188.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1188.name: Donald Trump
a1188.title: US President
a1188.speech: Had previously said that the presence of his Ukrainian counterpart, Volodymyr Zelensky, at the talks was not "very important." "He has been in meetings for three years and nothing has been done," he said in an interview with Fox Radio. "So I do not think it is very important for him to take part in meetings."

a1188.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1188.name: Donald Trump
a1188.title: US President
a1188.speech: Had described Zelensky as a "dictator without elections" and had already considered on Wednesday that the Russians had "taken a lot of territory" in Ukraine and therefore had "the cards in hand."

a1366.speaker: Linda Ofori-Kwafo, Chief of Party for the USAID/Ghana Performance Accountability Activity (PAA)
a1366.name: Linda Ofori-Kwafo
a1366.title: Chief of Party for the USAID/Ghana Performance Accountability Activity (PAA)
a1366.speech: Stated that due to the importance of media practitioners in championing the advocacy of quality and accountable public service delivery, it should be properly equipped; said through this, the media would be able to ensure that quality and accountable services were offered by assemblies and CSOs to the citizens they served ; "An informed media is essential for promoting accountability in public service delivery. By bridging the gap between journalists and CSOs, we are laying a strong foundation for sustainable and accountable governance at the district and community level."

a1366.speaker: Charles Yao Mawusi, Facilitator of the Trans-Media Network
a1366.name: Charles Yao Mawusi
a1366.title: Facilitator of the Trans-Media Network
a1366.speech: Emphasised the importance of advocacy by the media to ensure social justice and public involvement in all activities aimed at the improvement of the standard of living of the people; said it was the duty of the media to provide advocacy to ensure that the assemblies performed their duties for the quality of local public services across the country; and said the workshop aimed to provide the media practitioners with the right tools and knowledge to educate the citizenry on their roles in demanding responsive service delivery, efficient service delivery and adhering to quality standards for their benefit.

a1395.speaker: Germany (Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development, at bilateral consultations in Bamako)
a1395.name: Germany (Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development
a1395.title: at bilateral consultations in Bamako)
a1395.speech: Berlin confirmed the continuation of its support in the areas of water, agriculture and social protection, with an emphasis on rural areas and vulnerable populations. Germany reaffirmed its commitment to continuing its support to Mali, insisting on a partnership based on mutual respect and rigorous consideration of the new regional dynamics, notably the recent creation of the Confederation of Sahel States.

a1395.speaker: Malian and German authorities (joint outcome of the bilateral consultations)
a1395.name: Malian and German authorities (joint outcome of the bilateral consultations)
a1395.speech: The discussions welcomed the tangible results achieved through bilateral cooperation, in particular the rehabilitation of agricultural infrastructure in several regions and progress in improving access to drinking water. Despite a still very complex security context, the two parties reiterated their common desire to maintain a constructive dialogue and to develop their cooperation according to the concrete needs expressed by local communities. They agreed to extend their joint programming until 2026, with particular attention to isolated rural areas.

a1409.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
a1409.name: Daniel Chapo
a1409.title: President of the Republic of Mozambique
a1409.speech: According to Chapo, the North American administration reiterated its willingness to continue supporting Mozambique in the process of stabilisation and restoration of security in Cabo Delgado, through the strengthening of joint actions of training, technical assistance and intelligence sharing.

a1409.speaker: North American (US) companies
a1409.name: North American (US) companies
a1409.speech: During the working sessions, various North American companies expressed interest in expanding their investments in the country, with a focus on sectors that can serve as foundations for security and sustainable development.

a1409.speaker: Government of Mozambique
a1409.name: Government of Mozambique
a1409.speech: The government stated that the creation of economic opportunities and the strengthening of national skills form part of the integrated strategy for the stabilisation of Cabo Delgado ; underlined the joint commitment to deepen bilateral cooperation to combat terrorism, promote industrialisation and improve the living conditions of citizens, reiterating that peace and security are essential pillars for the country's economic future.

a1447.speaker: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, Djiboutian Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a1447.name: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf
a1447.title: Djiboutian Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a1447.speech: On the Francophonie: emphasised the need to preserve the political importance of the organisation while broadening its economic role. "I think the political dimensions of the Francophone space must be consolidated," he stressed, indicating that this space, which brings together nearly 90 countries, must evolve so that it can become a genuine engine of progress, development and solidarity among its members ; recalled that Djibouti is among the nations convinced that this organisation must maintain its political relevance while adapting to current economic realities: "We must not cast stones at the Francophone space. It is developing. It is evolving. And I believe we can only work further within the framework of this space" ; "That does not prevent States from having interests, regional and continental visions."

a1447.speaker: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, Djiboutian Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a1447.name: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf
a1447.title: Djiboutian Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a1447.speech: On Gaza/Palestine: "We have condemned the genocide under way in Gaza." ; "And it was not on 7 October that these abuses began. I believe the crisis must be taken globally and political solutions found to this problem that has persisted for 75 years. We cannot simply stop the clock at 7 October. I believe what is happening there is a genocide and it must be described as such." ; on South Africa's complaint accusing Israel of genocide before the International Court of Justice: "We have already done so and even before the ICC. Djibouti's position for more than 30 years has been the same. We wish for this conflict to stop, for the Palestinian people to be able to recover their rights and above all for the two-State solution to be genuinely enacted and implemented in order to stop the bloodbath" ; called for international awareness to put an end to the violence, denouncing the retreat of international law in the handling of this crisis.

a1447.speaker: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, Djiboutian Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a1447.name: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf
a1447.title: Djiboutian Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a1447.speech: On the African Union Commission: officially announced his candidacy for the presidency of the AU Commission, with the election scheduled for February 2025, and presented an ambitious vision for the future of the pan-African institution. "The African Union needs new leadership, focused on the implementation of decisions, transparency and above all financial autonomy to carry out its development projects," he stressed ; advocates an in-depth reform of the institution, notably on financing, asking that the Union's programmes be supported by member States themselves rather than depending on external funding, and insisted on the need to reform working methods and strengthen accountability within the Commission: "There is a lot of pedagogy to be done, leadership to be brought, especially on the innovation front. And so I fully intend to apply myself to this task" ; "Today, the Commission, the African Union needs a figure who has the necessary experience and lived experience of multilateral diplomacy and who above all is able to bring together African youth, the diaspora, women and place them at the centre of development. These are the challenges I intend to take up at the head of the Commission if I am elected in February 2025."

a1447.speaker: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, Djiboutian Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a1447.name: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf
a1447.title: Djiboutian Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a1447.speech: On regional stability and Ethiopia-Somalia tensions: stressed Djibouti's commitment, as current chair of the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD), to peace in the region. "We hope that the tension can subside. We have proposed an alternative to Ethiopia in order to avoid the region experiencing another crisis," he declared, then warned: "After Sudan, Somalia, South Sudan, a war between Ethiopia and Somalia would be catastrophic."

a1447.speaker: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, Djiboutian Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a1447.name: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf
a1447.title: Djiboutian Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a1447.speech: On the war in Sudan: reaffirmed Djibouti's commitment as a regional mediator. "We have already begun organising summits to try to bring about a mediation, to move towards a ceasefire. Three summits have been organised by Djibouti under the umbrella of IGAD. We organised a retreat in July, mediations and mediators. I myself intend to travel to Port Sudan very soon." ; "We have always hoped that Sudan could find a certain calm so that humanitarian aid can reach the populations in need," he added, before expressing his wish to see a political process emerge rapidly in order to stabilise this country, key to the region's balance.

a1514.speaker: Private creditors / bondholders
a1514.name: Private creditors / bondholders
a1514.speech: Have offered 333 million dollars in annual amortisation payments for a three-year extension; their response to Ethiopia's proposal of a four-year maturity extension, a four-year grace period and an interest rate cut to 5.1pc was lukewarm in initial virtual meetings.

a1514.speaker: Eyob Tekalegn, State Minister for Finance of Ethiopia
a1514.name: Eyob Tekalegn
a1514.title: State Minister for Finance of Ethiopia
a1514.speech: Contends that the default is not indicative of insolvency but rather a strategic alignment of debt servicing between bondholders and official creditors under the G20's Common Framework Agreement, which focuses on debt reprofiling from bilateral and private creditors.

a1514.speaker: World Bank International Debt Report
a1514.name: World Bank International Debt Report
a1514.speech: Shows the severity of the sovereign debt crisis among the world's poorest countries, with external debt service reaching a record high of 88.9 billion dollars in 2022.

a1770.speaker: Ministry of Health of Botswana (statement)
a1770.name: Ministry of Health of Botswana (statement)
a1770.speech: Stated that in the health sector, this aid comprised funding for direct service delivery and technical support, which has over the years been instrumental to the growth of the health sector of this country; that through support from PEPFAR, USAID and the CDC, the US has been part and parcel of the Botswana health story; that since the introduction of PEPFAR in 2003, the health sector has cumulatively benefited support amounting to more than One Billion Pula; and that the US support has been instrumental in helping Botswana to be one of the first countries in the world to reach and exceed the UNAIDS 95-95-95 targets well ahead of time, as a result of which many people living with HIV/AIDS in Botswana are able to live long.

a1794.speaker: Time Magazine (report)
a1794.name: Time Magazine (report)
a1794.speech: According to Time Magazine, tens of thousands of people had fled to safer grounds, including 438 relief camps nationwide, as water inundated more than 158,000 homes and destroyed 2,116 more.

a1794.speaker: Government of Myanmar
a1794.name: Government of Myanmar
a1794.speech: Said that tens of thousands of people had fled to safer grounds, including 438 relief camps nationwide, as water inundated more than 158,000 homes and destroyed 2,116 more.

a1794.speaker: Min Aung Hlaing, Myanmar junta chief (quoted by state media)
a1794.name: Min Aung Hlaing
a1794.title: Myanmar junta chief (quoted by state media)
a1794.speech: Made a rare request for foreign aid: "Officials from the government need to contact foreign countries to receive rescue and relief aid."

a1794.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (report)
a1794.name: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (report)
a1794.speech: Estimated 631,000 people were likely affected, and "multiple sources indicate that hundreds of people have died, with many more missing," the U.N. agency said in a report ; said evacuation and rescue efforts in Myanmar are ongoing, oftentimes hampered by damaged infrastructure, ongoing clashes and the lack of funds.

a1794.speaker: Thailand's disaster prevention department
a1794.name: Thailand's disaster prevention department
a1794.speech: According to the department, at least 45 have died from flooding and related incidents since mid-August, while about 28,000 households remain affected by the floods across 13 provinces.

a1794.speaker: Major General Zaw Min Tun, Myanmar junta spokesman
a1794.name: Major General Zaw Min Tun
a1794.title: Myanmar junta spokesman
a1794.speech: Said a thorough assessment of the damage will be made to provide support accordingly.

a1794.speaker: Myanmar's meteorology department
a1794.name: Myanmar's meteorology department
a1794.speech: Asked people near the river banks in three towns to flee to safer ground as the Sittaung River has exceeded its danger level by about five feet ; forecast heavy rains in three provinces including war-torn Rakhine State in the next 24 hours.

a1795.speaker: Dr Tapiwa Turambiswa, HIV/AIDS program manager at the Ministry of Health of Lesotho
a1795.name: Dr Tapiwa Turambiswa
a1795.title: HIV/AIDS program manager at the Ministry of Health of Lesotho
a1795.speech: Warned that the termination of USAID support, which amounted to over M852 million and had been earmarked for prevention efforts in 10 districts, through the Sustaining Epidemic Control through Unified Prevention (SECURE) Activity program, could lead to an increase in new HIV cases ; said the USAID funding cuts had impacted community prevention activities, condom distribution, Pre Exposure Prophylaxis – PrEP, Voluntary Male Medical Circumcision, and other critical services ; emphasized that the loss of HIV prevention funding could open the door for new HIV cases ; shared that since January this year, they had not received any funding for HIV prevention interventions, as the previous waiver funding only covered life-saving medication, that 93 percent of USAID funding had been paused, and that they had lost M168 million in funding from the USAID's "Bophelo bo Botle" (Healthy Life) treatment program ; "The funding termination has led to the retrenchment of 625 healthcare workers, including nurses, pharmacists, doctors, counsellors, psychologists, data clerks, and records assistants."

a1795.speaker: Dr Tapiwa Turambiswa, HIV/AIDS program manager at the Ministry of Health of Lesotho
a1795.name: Dr Tapiwa Turambiswa
a1795.title: HIV/AIDS program manager at the Ministry of Health of Lesotho
a1795.speech: Said Lesotho's HIV and tuberculosis (TB) programs had been heavily dependent on donor funding, with 86 percent of funding coming from international sources, making them unsustainable: "There is a great need for us to increase our domestic funding of these programs." ; "Additionally, Mr Trump's executive orders had adversely impacted health system strengthening, including treatment, care, and prevention activities for both HIV and TB."

a1795.speaker: Dr Tapiwa Turambiswa, HIV/AIDS program manager at the Ministry of Health of Lesotho
a1795.name: Dr Tapiwa Turambiswa
a1795.title: HIV/AIDS program manager at the Ministry of Health of Lesotho
a1795.speech: Said that while the Global Fund, a multilateral funding mechanism, is still providing support, they had also asked for a pause in major activities "as they reevaluate their funding model", and said that this was due to the US being the Global Fund's primary financier.

a1795.speaker: King Letsie III of Lesotho
a1795.name: King Letsie III of Lesotho
a1795.speech: Warned in a March interview with AFP that Lesotho could suffer significant economic consequences if President Trump followed through on proposed aid cuts and the termination of the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) trade agreement: "If AGOA is terminated, it will have an immediate impact on the economy because it could mean the loss of jobs for 30,000 to 40,000 people."

a1795.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1795.name: Donald Trump
a1795.title: US President
a1795.speech: Defended the aid cuts in March, saying of Lesotho, "it is a country nobody has ever heard of."

a1914.speaker: Abiola Bawuah, CEO of UBA Africa
a1914.name: Abiola Bawuah
a1914.title: CEO of UBA Africa
a1914.speech: After holding a meeting with the management of Caminhos de Ferro de Moçambique (CFM), assured that in the coming days agreements would be signed with CFM with the aim of driving the expansion of rail and port infrastructure: "In the coming months, perhaps one or two months from now, we should close a partnership agreement to see how we can support this enormous infrastructure and extension work they are about to carry out. Thus, we will give prominence to their expansion programme. We may partner with the Government to ensure that they expand the port and then perhaps renovate some equipment, locomotives that are old."

a1914.speaker: Abiola Bawuah, CEO of UBA Africa
a1914.name: Abiola Bawuah
a1914.title: CEO of UBA Africa
a1914.speech: "We have more than 60 million dollars in aid, which we use to support SMEs. Mozambicans are not excluded, they are part of it. And most of this happens in Africa. So SMEs have the right to support trade in Africa. So we have more than 60 million that we are using to support this. And this is a unique relationship between us and Africa."

a1914.speaker: Abiola Bawuah, CEO of UBA Africa
a1914.name: Abiola Bawuah
a1914.title: CEO of UBA Africa
a1914.speech: Explained, regarding her closed-door meeting with the investment administrator of the Bank of Mozambique, which she considered a moment of market assessment: "I think Mozambique is a very beautiful country. I saw that it is a major exporter of cashew. I also saw the beautiful hospitality industry. And then, as a bank, I think there is a great local opportunity. And that is part of the reason why I am here today. And this is to support all the people who want to invest in the main sectors of the economy."

a2176.speaker: United States Department of Homeland Security
a2176.name: United States Department of Homeland Security
a2176.speech: recently released the names and home addresses of 110 Liberians as the first batch of over 1500 Liberians to be evicted from the US, as part of the Trump Administration's crackdown on illegal immigration.

a2176.speaker: Trump administration
a2176.name: Trump administration
a2176.speech: has ordered a three-month pause on almost all foreign development assistance pending a review to see what fits in with the president's "America First" policy.

a2176.speaker: Aid groups and human rights watchdogs
a2176.name: Aid groups and human rights watchdogs
a2176.speech: warn that the freeze will put countless lives around the world at risk.

a2176.speaker: Cllr. Tiawan Saye Gongloe, Liberian human rights lawyer and political leader of the Liberian People's Party (LPP)
a2176.name: Cllr. Tiawan Saye Gongloe
a2176.title: Liberian human rights lawyer and political leader of the Liberian People's Party (LPP)
a2176.speech: is appealing to United States President Donald Trump against deporting Liberians and stopping the flow of US aid to Liberia; pleaded with President Trump to treat Liberia as a special case and urged the US President to respect the historical relationship and diplomatic ties between both countries ; "I want to appeal to U.S President Donald Trump to rethink his decision and treat Liberia as a special case regarding the planned mass deportation and aid halt to the world." ; "Liberia is a country that came out of the U.S historically and we are still trying to recover from war." ; many Liberians are in that category because they were escaping the war and seeking safety.

a2176.speaker: Cllr. Tiawan Saye Gongloe, political leader of the Liberian People's Party (LPP)
a2176.name: Cllr. Tiawan Saye Gongloe
a2176.title: political leader of the Liberian People's Party (LPP)
a2176.speech: Commenting on the issue of the aid halt, appealed that President Trump and the People of the U.S. consider Liberia because the country heavily relies on aid for development activities: "We want to also call on President Trump and the people of the U.S to consider Liberia on the issue of aid halt." ; "Liberia depends on aid for its education, health, and agricultural sectors, which are critical and most important to our heart." ; "We want you to consider us, not looking at the government's violation of human rights, corruption, and [violation of the] rule of law. Put us in a special category."

a2176.speaker: Cllr. Tiawan Saye Gongloe, political leader of the Liberian People's Party (LPP)
a2176.name: Cllr. Tiawan Saye Gongloe
a2176.title: political leader of the Liberian People's Party (LPP)
a2176.speech: called on Liberian President Joseph Nyuma Boakai to consider the topics of mass deportation and aid halt as a wake-up call: "I also want to call on President Boakai to take the topics of aid halt and mass deportation as a wakeup call to manage the country's resources well to the benefit of the majority of the Liberian people"; he urged President Boakai to pass an Executive Order reducing the salary and benefits of government officials from the over US$30,000 they are earning.

a2235.speaker: Harry Mokoka, African studies scholar at the University of Pretoria
a2235.name: Harry Mokoka
a2235.title: African studies scholar at the University of Pretoria
a2235.speech: "By crafting our own legal references, we're not only strengthening domestic systems, we're also changing how heritage is understood and valued globally." ; "This is part of a broader continental movement toward legal sovereignty, an assertion that we have the expertise, the mandate, and the lived experience to define what justice looks like for our heritage."

a2235.speaker: Harry Mokoka, African studies scholar at the University of Pretoria
a2235.name: Harry Mokoka
a2235.title: African studies scholar at the University of Pretoria
a2235.speech: Explained that "Most return negotiations today are bound by conventions that reflect colonial-era assumptions, not African values or priorities."

a2235.speaker: Harry Mokoka, African studies scholar at the University of Pretoria
a2235.name: Harry Mokoka
a2235.title: African studies scholar at the University of Pretoria
a2235.speech: Noted that "Many countries lack the archival infrastructure, museum capacity, or legal resourcing to absorb large-scale returns" ; "And while the Lomé initiative marks a major step, scaling its vision across 54 countries, each with different legal traditions, will require long-term coordination."

a2235.speaker: UNESCO
a2235.name: UNESCO
a2235.speech: According to UNESCO, since 2018 more than 20 African countries have adopted or drafted national restitution frameworks.

a2235.speaker: Kevin Nyambega, Kenya Cultural Centre
a2235.name: Kevin Nyambega
a2235.title: Kenya Cultural Centre
a2235.speech: "We're not just asking for artefacts to come home. We're defining the legal ground on which they return." ; "This is about authorship - about ensuring that our laws speak with our own voice."

a2235.speaker: Kevin Nyambega, Kenya Cultural Centre
a2235.name: Kevin Nyambega
a2235.title: Kenya Cultural Centre
a2235.speech: According to Nyambega, "Sacred objects, human remains, and ceremonial artefacts often carry meanings far deeper than ownership, yet existing legal systems tend to reduce them to commodities or museum property." ; "That's why the shift underway is as philosophical as it is procedural."

a2235.speaker: Fatoumata Diakité, cultural law expert based in Mali
a2235.name: Fatoumata Diakité
a2235.title: cultural law expert based in Mali
a2235.speech: "What we're seeing is the emergence of African legal consciousness around heritage. This is not just about what returns, but how it returns, and who gets to write that story." ; "Restitution isn't only about artefacts. It's about restoring legal dignity. Restoring the power to name, to protect, and to decide."

a2303.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) (statement)
a2303.name: World Food Programme (WFP) (statement)
a2303.speech: said that shortly after crossing the last checkpoint beyond the Zikim crossing into Gaza, the convoy (of 25 trucks) encountered enormous crowds of civilians anxiously waiting to access food supplies. "As the convoy approached, the crowd around it came under fire from Israeli tanks, snipers and other gunfire," states the WFP note, which deeply lamented Sunday's "tragic incident" that resulted in the loss of "countless lives." ; "Today's [Sunday's] violent incident occurred despite assurances from the Israeli authorities that conditions for humanitarian operations would improve; among them, that the armed forces would not be present nor engage in clashes at any point along the routes of the humanitarian convoys." ; The organisation reiterated that armed groups must "never" be present near or aboard its humanitarian aid convoys.

a2303.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a2303.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a2303.speech: Around 90,000 women and children need urgent treatment for malnutrition in Gaza, while one in three people has not eaten for days, according to the WFP.

a2303.speaker: Israeli army
a2303.name: Israeli army
a2303.speech: admitted having fired "warning shots" and being aware of casualties, but stated on Sunday that the reported death toll did not match the information available to the forces.

a2535.speaker: Kassim Haroun Ali, Minister Delegate in charge of Decentralisation of Djibouti
a2535.name: Kassim Haroun Ali
a2535.title: Minister Delegate in charge of Decentralisation of Djibouti
a2535.speech: In his welcome and thank-you speech, the Minister stressed the importance of the collaboration between USAID and the Ministry Delegate in charge of Decentralisation. He also highlighted the realisation of this collaboration through the Civil Society Engagement Support Project, which is called upon to play fully its role as an actor in the country's development ; The Minister recalled the constant support his ministry provides to the Regional Councils as well as to the local Development Committees, which are associations entirely dedicated to local development.

a2535.speaker: Nancy Ostrowski, USAID representative
a2535.name: Nancy Ostrowski
a2535.title: USAID representative
a2535.speech: For her part, the USAID Representative stressed the key role of the Ministry Delegate in charge of Decentralisation in the Civil Society Engagement Support Project and reiterated USAID's support ; The Representative thanked Minister Kassim Haroun Ali for his exemplary commitment and welcomed the excellent collaboration between the KAIZEN company and the MDCD.

a2771.speaker: Itai Siabulembu, conservationist with ZimParks and area manager at Chizarira National Park
a2771.name: Itai Siabulembu
a2771.title: conservationist with ZimParks and area manager at Chizarira National Park
a2771.speech: "This is a game-changer for Mucheni." ; "By reintroducing these animals, we are restoring the ecological balance and setting the stage for economic opportunities through eco-tourism and conservation employment."

a2771.speaker: Local leaders and community members
a2771.name: Local leaders and community members
a2771.speech: Have welcomed the project as a long-awaited boost to their conservation efforts.

a2771.speaker: Elmon Mudenda, senior village head
a2771.name: Elmon Mudenda
a2771.title: senior village head
a2771.speech: "Our people have always lived alongside wildlife, and this project strengthens that bond." ; "There is no conservancy without animals. With wildlife back in Mucheni, we can dream again of jobs, tourists visiting and passing on this heritage to our children."

a2771.speaker: Mthokozisi Dlodlo, SWM wildlife ecologist
a2771.name: Mthokozisi Dlodlo
a2771.title: SWM wildlife ecologist
a2771.speech: "This is not just about moving animals; it's about restoring ecosystems, building climate resilience, and empowering people." ; "The introduction of these species is expected to attract predators and additional wildlife, fostering a balanced and thriving ecosystem."

a2788.speaker: Bill Gates, Gates Foundation Chair
a2788.name: Bill Gates
a2788.title: Gates Foundation Chair
a2788.speech: “Humanity is at a crossroads. With millions of children's lives on the line, global leaders have a once-in-a-generation chance to do something extraordinary. The choices they make now—whether to go forward with proposed steep cuts to health aid or to give the world's children the chance they deserve to live a healthy life—will determine what kind of future we leave the next generation.” ; “What's happening to the health of the world's children is worse than most people realize, but our long-term prospects are better than most people can imagine.” ; “I don't expect most governments to suddenly restore foreign aid to historic levels, but I am an optimist, and I believe governments can and will do what's needed to save as many children as possible.”

a2788.speaker: Bill Gates, Gates Foundation Chair
a2788.name: Bill Gates
a2788.title: Gates Foundation Chair
a2788.speech: “We have a roadmap for saving millions of children and making some of the deadliest childhood diseases history by 2045. I'm urging world leaders to invest in the health of all people, especially children, to deliver this future.”

a2788.speaker: Bill Gates, Gates Foundation Chair
a2788.name: Bill Gates
a2788.title: Gates Foundation Chair
a2788.speech: Announced his foundation's pledge of $912 million over three years to the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria's 2026-2028 replenishment. “An entire generation is alive today thanks to the world's generosity, smart investments, and the hard work of governments and Global Fund partners. Now, we must go further so the next generation grows up in a world where no child dies from preventable causes.”

a2788.speaker: Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) study
a2788.name: Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) study
a2788.speech: According to a recent study by the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME), global development assistance for health fell by 21% between 2024 and 2025, and is now at a 15-year low.

a2788.speaker: Gates Foundation and IHME (research results)
a2788.name: Gates Foundation and IHME (research results)
a2788.speech: Results from work by the Gates Foundation and the IHME indicate that sustaining global investments in child health and scaling lifesaving innovations could cut child deaths in half again over the next 20 years.

a2788.speaker: Dawda Jobarteh, deputy director of the Gates Foundation's Goalkeepers campaign
a2788.name: Dawda Jobarteh
a2788.title: deputy director of the Gates Foundation's Goalkeepers campaign
a2788.speech: “Every year, Goalkeepers unites changemakers to inspire and push one another forward. Together, we can reimagine a future without preventable child deaths and unlock the next wave of breakthroughs for the world's children.”

a2788.speaker: Jon Batiste, singer and musical curator, and Olivia Wilde, actress and director (event co-hosts)
a2788.name: Jon Batiste
a2788.title: singer and musical curator, and Olivia Wilde, actress and director (event co-hosts)
a2788.speech: Urged the audience to remember that while the world has made progress, “we can't stop at almost,” which was the event's theme.

a2817.speaker: Many experts
a2817.name: Many experts
a2817.speech: Described this development as a wake-up call for Nigeria to reduce reliance on foreign aid and take full ownership of its HIV response alongside other public health needs.

a2817.speaker: Nigerian government, through the National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a2817.name: Nigerian government
a2817.title: through the National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a2817.speech: Announced plans to locally produce HIV-related medical tools, including test kits and antiretroviral drugs.

a2817.speaker: Wale Edun, Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy
a2817.name: Wale Edun
a2817.title: Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy
a2817.speech: According to him, the government also approved N4.8 billion for HIV treatment; the additional allocation, equivalent to $200 million, will target health programmes such as Tuberculosis, HIV, Malaria and Polio.

a2817.speaker: US Department of State
a2817.name: US Department of State
a2817.speech: According to the US Department of State, PEPFAR is Nigeria's primary funding source for antiretroviral therapy, testing, and prevention services ; data from the US Department of State website shows that between 2015 and 2024 the US provided $2.28 billion (N3.4 trillion) in HIV/AIDS assistance to Nigeria, approximately 53.21 per cent of Nigeria's total health budget over that period.

a2817.speaker: Experts
a2817.name: Experts
a2817.speech: Argue that Nigeria needs a much larger and more consistent financial commitment to effectively combat HIV/AIDS ; experts remain sceptical about Nigeria's ability to fully fund and sustain the local production initiative.

a2817.speaker: Multiple reports and studies
a2817.name: Multiple reports and studies
a2817.speech: Showed that the government struggled to increase domestic funding enough to cover the gap created by PEPFAR's reduction of about $83 million in yearly programme support between 2011 and 2015, with key areas of the HIV response suffering, such as the availability of antiretroviral drugs, testing services, and healthcare infrastructure.

a2817.speaker: Victor Adepoju, director of HIV, Viral Hepatitis and Infectious Diseases at Jhpiego, an affiliate of Johns Hopkins University
a2817.name: Victor Adepoju
a2817.title: director of HIV, Viral Hepatitis and Infectious Diseases at Jhpiego, an affiliate of Johns Hopkins University
a2817.speech: Believes that Nigeria will need a different funding model to sustain its HIV/AIDS response if PEPFAR funding is withdrawn ; said one significant step the country has taken is establishing an integrated Technical Working Group (TWG) for HIV, TB and Malaria ; argued that while Western donors previously funded these programmes separately, the approach made them less efficient and more costly, and noted that by integrating efforts Nigeria can cut costs and improve programme efficiency ; highlights the need for local production of TB, HIV and malaria drugs, which could lower treatment costs and enhance sustainability ; cautions that Nigeria may still struggle to independently fund the HIV response given its current national budget: “Nigeria won't be able to fully sustain (the programme) given the need, but will be able to salvage some” ; noted that Nigeria recently approved the procurement of HIV drugs for 150,000 people, while over one million people rely on treatment, warning “Many will still die” ; stressed that local drug manufacturing is still a future-focused solution that does not address the immediate funding gap, and suggested expanding health insurance, attracting private sector investment, and creating a safety net for vulnerable populations who cannot afford treatment.

a2817.speaker: Dan Onwujekwe, former principal investigator at PEPFAR and research fellow at the Nigerian Institute of Medical Research (NIMR)
a2817.name: Dan Onwujekwe
a2817.title: former principal investigator at PEPFAR and research fellow at the Nigerian Institute of Medical Research (NIMR)
a2817.speech: Revealed that international donor agencies had warned Nigeria as far back as 2012 to prepare for a potential pullout ; noted in an earlier interview with Punch newspaper that between 2012 and 2015 PEPFAR repeatedly engaged with Nigerian health authorities, advising them on strategies for transitioning to domestic ownership of diagnostics, drugs, equipment and infrastructure ; said that despite these warnings little was done, leading to current shortages of TB/HIV drugs, especially for persons over 40 years old living with HIV/AIDS: “It is going to be a big challenge despite the early warnings” ; “They (PEPFAR) gave Nigeria three years of notice, holding multiple meetings on the transition process and suggesting ways to take ownership.”

a2817.speaker: Dan Onwujekwe, former principal investigator at PEPFAR and research fellow at the Nigerian Institute of Medical Research (NIMR)
a2817.name: Dan Onwujekwe
a2817.title: former principal investigator at PEPFAR and research fellow at the Nigerian Institute of Medical Research (NIMR)
a2817.speech: Warned that losing donor support could cripple Nigeria's HIV/AIDS control efforts and called for urgent government action at all levels ; urged the authorities to designate a specific tax allocation — such as a portion of stamp duty — to fund TB and HIV programmes, emphasising that failure to act would be disastrous for a country with one of the highest burdens of TB and HIV globally.

a2829.speaker: John Siafa, Monrovia City Mayor
a2829.name: John Siafa
a2829.title: Monrovia City Mayor
a2829.speech: Says revenue collection at the institution is progressing: “Currently, more than eight hundred-eleven thousand US Dollars is being generated by the MCC.” ; told the ELBC on Monday, October 21, 2024 that more than one-point-four million US Dollars invoices are being issued as part of efforts to contribute to the Country's revenue envelop ; also disclosed ongoing plans to increase revenue collection at the MCC in 2025.

a2829.speaker: John Siafa, Monrovia City Mayor
a2829.name: John Siafa
a2829.title: Monrovia City Mayor
a2829.speech: Has reaffirmed the Government's commitment to prioritizing sanitation under its development ARREST Agenda.

a3024.speaker: Noah Salakae, Minister of Transport and Infrastructure of Botswana
a3024.name: Noah Salakae
a3024.title: Minister of Transport and Infrastructure of Botswana
a3024.speech: In his keynote address to the summit: “Transport doesn’t mine the minerals, but it moves them, exports them, and delivers their value to the people” ; “The greatest bottleneck to scaling up Botswana’s mining exports is not under the ground – it is above it.”

a3024.speaker: Noah Salakae, Minister of Transport and Infrastructure of Botswana
a3024.name: Noah Salakae
a3024.title: Minister of Transport and Infrastructure of Botswana
a3024.speech: Made clear that Botswana is “actively exploring infrastructure bonds, including green and sustainability-linked bonds” to unlock private capital ; “We are establishing modalities such as shadow tolling, cost-sharing arrangements, and user-pays principles,” drawing from global examples such as Chile’s mining royalty infrastructure funds, India’s viability gap corridors, and Australia’s mine-to-port user models.

a3024.speaker: Noah Salakae, Minister of Transport and Infrastructure of Botswana
a3024.name: Noah Salakae
a3024.title: Minister of Transport and Infrastructure of Botswana
a3024.speech: “We must stop seeing ourselves as landlocked. We are land-linked. Our infrastructure must reflect that.”

a3024.speaker: Noah Salakae, Minister of Transport and Infrastructure of Botswana
a3024.name: Noah Salakae
a3024.title: Minister of Transport and Infrastructure of Botswana
a3024.speech: Called for “a smart mining economy with smart logistics”, with smart permits, real-time cargo tracking and digital customs on the government’s radar.

a3024.speaker: Noah Salakae, Minister of Transport and Infrastructure of Botswana
a3024.name: Noah Salakae
a3024.title: Minister of Transport and Infrastructure of Botswana
a3024.speech: Ended his speech with a challenge to the mining industry: “Help us design and pay for the logistics of tomorrow. The days of subsidised infrastructure are over. Work with us – or watch the opportunity pass you by.”

a3024.speaker: A recent position paper
a3024.name: A recent position paper
a3024.speech: Estimates that to replace just P23 billion in lost diamond revenues, the private sector must double profits, triple exports, and create at least 200,000 new jobs.

a3127.speaker: Dr Esi Sey, Project Director of YALI RLC
a3127.name: Dr Esi Sey
a3127.title: Project Director of YALI RLC
a3127.speech: Described the cohort as “passionate individuals with innovative solutions.”

a3127.speaker: Michael Ackon, Ghanaian student leader and YALI award recipient (post)
a3127.name: Michael Ackon
a3127.title: Ghanaian student leader and YALI award recipient (post)
a3127.speech: In his post expressed gratitude to the YALI RLC West Africa team, USAID, facilitators, and fellow participants, emphasizing the program’s transformative impact on his leadership skills and network. “I’m committed to leveraging this experience to advance public policy initiatives benefiting Ghana and Africa,” he said.

a3241.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States of America (post on the social network Truth)
a3241.name: Donald Trump
a3241.title: President of the United States of America (post on the social network Truth)
a3241.speech: Suggests the annulment of the judicial proceedings against Benjamin Netanyahu in Israel for corruption, considering the act a "witch hunt" against "a great hero," and states that the United States will save him ; says he has been informed that Netanyahu was summoned to court on Monday to answer a case dating from May 2020 and suggests that it should be annulled, or that a pardon should be granted to the prime minister ; added that it was the United States of America that saved Israel and that it will now save Bibi Netanyahu ; criticised the fact that the hearings are continuing at a moment when Israel has just experienced "one of the greatest moments in its history," referring to the bombardments and retaliations with Iran.

a3241.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel
a3241.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
a3241.title: Prime Minister of Israel
a3241.speech: Denies the accusations and says it is a political attempt to remove him from power.

a3522.speaker: Bank stress tests (central bank)
a3522.name: Bank stress tests (central bank)
a3522.speech: Stress tests reveal that if the 10 largest depositors pulled out, 20 of 29 banks would miss liquidity requirements.

a3522.speaker: Ethiopian banking regulators
a3522.name: Ethiopian banking regulators
a3522.speech: Have told smaller banks to raise capital to five billion Br by June 2026, convinced that forced consolidation may create larger but still brittle banks.

a3522.speaker: National Bank of Ethiopia (Central Bank)
a3522.name: National Bank of Ethiopia (Central Bank)
a3522.speech: Warning that a sudden withdrawal by top depositors could trigger chaos overnight.

a3522.speaker: Abiy Ahmed (PhD), Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a3522.name: Abiy Ahmed (PhD)
a3522.title: Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a3522.speech: Recent claim that access to the Red Sea is “existential” for Ethiopia has raised hackles across the Horn of Africa; his declaration to "correct the mistake of landlocked status” led Eritrea to welcome Egyptian and Saudi investment in the port of Assab.

a3522.speaker: Federal Government of Ethiopia
a3522.name: Federal Government of Ethiopia
a3522.speech: On July 28, 2024, announced a historic liberalisation of the foreign-exchange regime, under which the Birr would supposedly float, with its value determined by market forces.

a3610.speaker: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera, President of Malawi
a3610.name: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera
a3610.title: President of Malawi
a3610.speech: Urged the newly appointed Senior Counsel to live up to the highest ideals of loyalty, integrity, and professional excellence, which he described as the foundational pillars for national transformation, and warned that the honour of being named Senior Counsel comes with a lifelong burden of leadership by example: “You are now the example to the whole nation. And I myself will rely on you for counsel and wisdom as I continue to lead this country without compromising these values.” ; Challenged the new appointees not to become complacent or rest on their laurels, stressing that their actions going forward will either uplift or betray the trust bestowed upon them: “From now on, you cannot afford to drop the ball.”

a3610.speaker: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera, President of Malawi
a3610.name: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera
a3610.title: President of Malawi
a3610.speech: Issued a national challenge calling for a culture of patriotic duty across all professions and rebuked the widespread belief that money, power, prayer, or foreign aid alone can fix Malawi’s problems: “We need a nation of citizens who are loyal—not to individuals or tribes, but to the country, its laws, and their professional duty. That loyalty, that unshakeable devotion to Malawi, is what I saw in you when I made these appointments.”

a3610.speaker: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera, President of Malawi
a3610.name: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera
a3610.title: President of Malawi
a3610.speech: Defined integrity as the refusal to cut corners or tolerate mediocrity, calling it the antidote to Malawi’s chronic underdevelopment, and on ability said: “It means that when the time comes to execute, you do not hesitate—and you do not fail.”

a3671.speaker: Nasteho, displaced mother in Hilac IDP camp, Dusamareb
a3671.name: Nasteho
a3671.title: displaced mother in Hilac IDP camp, Dusamareb
a3671.speech: “We don’t have enough food. My children eat in the morning, and then I go to the forest to collect firewood. It’s a long walk, and the firewood is far from town now. There’s danger in the forest so I go with other people and if they leave me there, I fear for my safety,” she told Radio Ergo.

a3671.speaker: Nasteho, displaced mother in Hilac IDP camp, Dusamareb
a3671.name: Nasteho
a3671.title: displaced mother in Hilac IDP camp, Dusamareb
a3671.speech: On her debt to a local restaurant: “Sometimes they threaten to take the firewood in place of money, which is upsetting. I’ve had to delay payments three times already, and this month is the final deadline,” she explained.

a3671.speaker: Nasteho, displaced mother in Hilac IDP camp, Dusamareb
a3671.name: Nasteho
a3671.title: displaced mother in Hilac IDP camp, Dusamareb
a3671.speech: On her shelter: “It’s a small, fragile hut. Every few weeks, we need to repair it, but we don’t have the materials. The heat is unbearable, and when it rains, the roof leaks. I can’t protect my children or myself from the weather,” she said.

a3671.speaker: Ayni Hussein Abdullahi, single mother of seven in Hilac camp
a3671.name: Ayni Hussein Abdullahi
a3671.title: single mother of seven in Hilac camp
a3671.speech: “Sometimes we go without food. We used to eat three meals a day, but now we’re lucky if we eat once. It’s not like before when we had enough,” Ayni said.

a3671.speaker: Ayni Hussein Abdullahi, single mother of seven in Hilac camp
a3671.name: Ayni Hussein Abdullahi
a3671.title: single mother of seven in Hilac camp
a3671.speech: Explained that while she’s away looking for work, her children are left alone and often hungry: “We borrow food from our neighbours, and that’s how we manage to cook. But when you’ve left your children behind, they’re left to fend for themselves and sometimes they have nothing to eat. The next day, if I manage to find work, I try to repay the debt, but there are times when neighbours refuse to lend us anything until the previous debt is cleared. Sometimes the kids go without food in the morning and dinner at night. We just hope that the next day will be better,” she said.

a3671.speaker: Hassan Salad Gelle, Hilac camp chairman
a3671.name: Hassan Salad Gelle
a3671.title: Hilac camp chairman
a3671.speech: Said the conditions have worsened since the aid stopped, with families forced to share whatever little they have to survive ; “The aid agencies, like WFP, say they’re running out of funds due to the large number of displaced people. They promised us two months ago that they would resume assistance, but we haven’t heard anything since,” Hassan told Radio Ergo.

a3898.speaker: Ivan Manhiça, permanent secretary of the Mozambican Health Ministry
a3898.name: Ivan Manhiça
a3898.title: permanent secretary of the Mozambican Health Ministry
a3898.speech: Said the increase in cases of tuberculosis has been influenced by the cut in international funding for the health sector. “Mozambique continues to face a high burden of this disease, often associated with HIV, affecting mainly the most vulnerable populations, requiring coordinated actions, continuous investments and technological innovations for early diagnosis and effective treatment” ; explained that some regions are beginning to see an increase in the number of cases, following “the cut in funding from the United States Agency for International Development (USAID)”.

a3898.speaker: Ivan Manhiça, permanent secretary of the Mozambican Health Ministry
a3898.name: Ivan Manhiça
a3898.title: permanent secretary of the Mozambican Health Ministry
a3898.speech: Also said that the abandonment of treatment continues to be one of the biggest causes of death. “Looking at the incidence in the general population, there are 361 cases per 100,000 inhabitants. With the real estimates, we expect to find about 121,000 cases of tuberculosis per year.”

a3898.speaker: Francisco Saúte, director of the Manhiça Health Research Centre (CISM)
a3898.name: Francisco Saúte
a3898.title: director of the Manhiça Health Research Centre (CISM)
a3898.speech: Said that research laboratories are working to find a new vaccine for tuberculosis in order to prevent infections from spreading easily. “I must first say that there is a tuberculosis vaccine, which is more than 100 years old, but it has limited efficacy in preventing infections. We're investigating a new one, using more recent technologies and we're still in the initial evaluation phase. We're waiting for specific measures to be completed in order to finalize the preliminary analysis of the data” ; guaranteed that CISM will soon test the new vaccine to prevent tuberculosis, “which is at the sample collection stage.”

a4019.speaker: Ambassadors of the European Union member states accredited in Mozambique
a4019.name: Ambassadors of the European Union member states accredited in Mozambique
a4019.speech: Reaffirmed today in Maputo their unconditional support and the strengthening of the partnership in the structural reforms under way in the country, and the political commitment to an inclusive national dialogue, which include the stabilisation of the situation of terrorist attacks in Cabo Delgado province and the modernisation of the Mozambican economy.

a4019.speaker: Antonino Maggiore, European Union Ambassador to Mozambique
a4019.name: Antonino Maggiore
a4019.title: European Union Ambassador to Mozambique
a4019.speech: Said that the signing of the political commitment with opposition parties, the meetings with civil society and with the former presidential candidate Venâncio Mondlane close one stage and open a new page in the country: “We welcome the openness and clear acknowledgement with which the President identified the problems and challenges the country faces.”

a4019.speaker: Antonino Maggiore, European Union Ambassador to Mozambique
a4019.name: Antonino Maggiore
a4019.title: European Union Ambassador to Mozambique
a4019.speech: Noted that, within the framework of the reforms under way in the country, the government can count on the European Union and the member states, which are fully available to make their contribution: “We are working with the government and the institutions for comprehensive and concrete support, directed at the implementation of the political commitment to inclusive dialogue. We want to grant that support not only to the government, but also clearly to civil society and to the leaders of the opposition parties.”

a4019.speaker: Antonino Maggiore, European Union Ambassador to Mozambique
a4019.name: Antonino Maggiore
a4019.title: European Union Ambassador to Mozambique
a4019.speech: Stressed that the reform process — including economic reform, the electoral package, fiscal reform, corruption, digitalisation and the police, the latter with a view to overcoming violence and guaranteeing respect for human rights — comprises aspects the European Union considers fundamental; and made it known that the EU’s partnership is unique, comprehensive and 360 degrees across all areas regarded as priorities for the country, with an integrated approach based on support for development, humanitarian aid and security.

a4066.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) statement
a4066.name: World Food Programme (WFP) statement
a4066.speech: Said yesterday it was suspending aid for 650 000 malnourished women and children in Ethiopia because of a lack of funding: “WFP is being forced to halt treatment for 650 000 malnourished women and children in May due to insufficient funding” ; “WFP had planned to reach two million mothers and children with life-saving nutrition assistance in 2025” ; warned they were among 3.6 million people in Ethiopia who would no longer get food aid in the coming weeks without urgent new funding.

a4066.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a4066.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a4066.speech: Said more than 10 million people are facing hunger in the east African country of around 130 million, and that it was facing a shortfall of US$222 million for the April-September period in Ethiopia.

a4146.speaker: Joint FAO-WFP report (Early Warning Analysis of Acute Food Insecurity Hotspots)
a4146.name: Joint FAO-WFP report (Early Warning Analysis of Acute Food Insecurity Hotspots)
a4146.speech: Raised the alarm on 20 countries including Ethiopia, saying that acute food insecurity levels appear to be reaching new highs globally as a result of the socio-economic fallout of measures imposed to contain the spread of COVID-19 ; warned that hotspots in four countries – Burkina Faso, Yemen, South Sudan and Nigeria – are on the brink of severe levels of food insecurity and could potentially fall into famine within three to six months as the coronavirus pandemic erodes people’s ability to access food ; found that millions of people who were already facing hunger are on the brink of famine as the pandemic plunders employment, disrupts agricultural activities, slashes remittances and sends crude prices spiralling.

a4146.speaker: Margot van der Velden, WFP director of emergencies
a4146.name: Margot van der Velden
a4146.title: WFP director of emergencies
a4146.speech: “We are at a catastrophic turning point. Once again, we face the risk of famine in four different parts of the world at the same time.”

a4146.speaker: 2020 Global Report on Food Crises – September 2020 update
a4146.name: 2020 Global Report on Food Crises – September 2020 update
a4146.speech: According to the report, the COVID-19 pandemic has exacerbated these pre-existing and on-going drivers, mainly by causing economic activities to decline, which in turn led to income loss and reduced household purchasing power, and a multitude of food-system wide shocks.

a4149.speaker: OPEC Secretariat (calculations)
a4149.name: OPEC Secretariat (calculations)
a4149.speech: According to OPEC Secretariat calculations, the price of the OPEC basket of 12 crudes stood at $74.12 a barrel on Tuesday, March 18, 2025, compared with $73.65 the previous day.

a4220.speaker: Hilderbrand Shayo, participant representing TIB Development Bank (opinion article)
a4220.name: Hilderbrand Shayo
a4220.title: participant representing TIB Development Bank (opinion article)
