a4220.speech: Writes that the policy dialogue convened by the Economic and Social Research Foundation (ESRF) signals the deepening of Beijing’s support for least developed countries, including Tanzania; recommends that Tanzanian leaders consider Prof Li Xiaoyun’s book as lessons “particularly relevant as Tanzania embarks on its Dira 2050 journey” ; notes that many developing countries, including Tanzania, are experiencing shrinking aid flows from traditional donors, illustrated by the winding down of USAID’s operations, and that this shift calls for new strategies and greater reliance on homegrown solutions and South–South cooperation, with TIB Development Bank positioned to explore and champion alternative development financing models suitable for the realities of the Global South.

a4220.speaker: Prof Li Xiaoyun, Chair, Professor and Honorary Dean of CIDGA, China Agricultural University (author of The End of Poverty and the Taming of Inequality)
a4220.name: Prof Li Xiaoyun
a4220.title: Chair, Professor and Honorary Dean of CIDGA, China Agricultural University (author of The End of Poverty and the Taming of Inequality)
a4220.speech: His book offers a compelling call to action: empower individuals to take charge of their futures, backed by effective government and societal support; it details the multi-dimensional nature of poverty and the comprehensive strategies needed to reduce inequality ; he argues that poverty is not a remote or isolated issue, but a collective challenge that requires holistic, people-centred solutions, and encourages policymakers and citizens alike to rethink their roles and interventions.

a4247.speaker: Russell Dlamini, Prime Minister of Eswatini
a4247.name: Russell Dlamini
a4247.title: Prime Minister of Eswatini
a4247.speech: Opened the event by expressing his profound pride and humility in hosting the historic occasion; emphasised that the launch reaffirms a collective commitment to “building a safer, resilient, and sustainable future for our region.”

a4247.speaker: Russell Dlamini, Prime Minister of Eswatini
a4247.name: Russell Dlamini
a4247.title: Prime Minister of Eswatini
a4247.speech: Highlighted the urgency of addressing drought, describing it as a “silent crisis” that has historically shaped the region's development and continues to threaten livelihoods, economies, and ecosystems; recalled the devastating 2015–2016 El Niño-induced drought that left nearly half of Eswatini's population in need of humanitarian assistance, costing approximately E3.84 billion, about 19 per cent of the national budget at the time and 7 per cent of GDP, an experience that underscored the limitations of reactive disaster responses, which are “too costly, both in resources and in human suffering.”

a4247.speaker: Russell Dlamini, Prime Minister of Eswatini
a4247.name: Russell Dlamini
a4247.title: Prime Minister of Eswatini
a4247.speech: Detailed the “Eswatini Water Supply and Sanitation Access Project,” financed through a World Bank loan, which improved water access in the drought-prone Shiselweni region; reported that most project deliverables have been achieved or are nearing completion, including water infrastructure, risk profiles, municipal drought management plans and the Composite Drought Index – Eswatini (CDI-E); and said the National Drought Policy ensures that “planning, budgeting and implementation across sectors are informed by risk and sustainable efforts.”

a4247.speaker: Russell Dlamini, Prime Minister of Eswatini
a4247.name: Russell Dlamini
a4247.title: Prime Minister of Eswatini
a4247.speech: Cited the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015–2030), which advocates understanding risk, strengthening governance, investing in resilience, and building back better; also referenced the 2015 Paris Agreement's call to limit global warming while supporting climate adaptation, as well as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, and said Eswatini aligns with the SADC Disaster Risk Management Strategy and Action Plan 2022, recognising that “only through collective action can we address the shared risks that transcend our borders.”

a4247.speaker: Russell Dlamini, Prime Minister of Eswatini
a4247.name: Russell Dlamini
a4247.title: Prime Minister of Eswatini
a4247.speech: Said the new platforms will facilitate “dialogue, coordination, and joint action,” bringing together governments, communities, civil society, the private sector, academia, and development partners to co-create solutions that are “regional in scope but speaking to local realities”, and will act as conduits for information dissemination and governance enhancement in disaster risk reduction.

a4247.speaker: Russell Dlamini, Prime Minister of Eswatini
a4247.name: Russell Dlamini
a4247.title: Prime Minister of Eswatini
a4247.speech: Urged the University of Eswatini, the World Bank, and the SADC Secretariat to collaborate closely with the National Disaster Management Agency (NDMA) to operationalise the Eswatini Drought Centre of Excellence for the benefit of the entire African continent.

a4247.speaker: Russell Dlamini, Prime Minister of Eswatini
a4247.name: Russell Dlamini
a4247.title: Prime Minister of Eswatini
a4247.speech: Praised the World Bank Group for helping Eswatini shift its perspective on drought from a mere disaster response issue to a broader development initiative; expressed pride in the NDMA's central role in resilience building, noting that its experience offers valuable lessons for institutions both locally and beyond.

a4247.speaker: Russell Dlamini, Prime Minister of Eswatini
a4247.name: Russell Dlamini
a4247.title: Prime Minister of Eswatini
a4247.speech: Painted a vision of a future where communities “anticipate risks and respond early and appropriately,” where regional solidarity is a “lived reality,” and where innovation in risk financing, social protection and water management empowers people to “withstand shocks and continue to thrive in the face of multiple hazards” ; “Let it be said that in Ezulwini, the ‘Valley of Heaven,’ in the Kingdom of Eswatini, we chose to strengthen our resolve, reinforced our partnerships, and raised our ambition” ; “When the roots are deep, there is no reason to fear the wind.”

a4347.speaker: Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a4347.name: Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a4347.speech: Urges donor countries to step up their support for displaced people in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DR Congo) ahead of the Great Lakes Conference in Paris.

a4347.speaker: Eric Batonon, NRC's Country Director for DR Congo
a4347.name: Eric Batonon
a4347.title: NRC's Country Director for DR Congo
a4347.speech: "We urgently need two things to support the most vulnerable people in DR Congo: unimpeded access and adequate funding that supports both immediate relief and long-term recovery," ; "The Great Lakes Conference is a crucial opportunity for States to push for safe, unhindered access by road, by air, and by reducing administrative barriers, so that aid can reach those most in need. At the same time, states must commit to increased and sustained funding. The conference must deliver more than words. It must deliver hope - and real commitments - for the millions of Congolese who have endured decades of conflict and neglect."

a4347.speaker: Eric Batonon, NRC's Country Director for DR Congo
a4347.name: Eric Batonon
a4347.title: NRC's Country Director for DR Congo
a4347.speech: "DR Congo is one of the most horrific examples of the consequences of the lack of funding for aid, which is hitting neglected crises hard. Of the 21 million people in the country in need of humanitarian support, fewer than seven million are currently targeted for assistance - and even that plan remains severely underfunded," ; "The human cost is staggering. Many children have no access to education, displaced families are left without a proper roof over their heads or access to clean water and sanitation. There is also insufficient investment in protection and local conflict resolution." ; "The current humanitarian funding for DR Congo equals about five cent per person in need per day. It is a stark illustration of the international community's neglect of this mega crisis. It's time to turn this around."

a4347.speaker: NRC annual list of the world's most neglected displacement crises (report)
a4347.name: NRC annual list of the world's most neglected displacement crises (report)
a4347.speech: For nine consecutive years, the DR Congo has featured on NRC's annual list of the world's most neglected displacement crises.

a4347.speaker: Chantale Tsesi Ndangosi, Director of the Amani Gok Primary School in Djugu, Ituri
a4347.name: Chantale Tsesi Ndangosi
a4347.title: Director of the Amani Gok Primary School in Djugu, Ituri
a4347.speech: Described the impossible conditions teachers and pupils face: "Our school was destroyed by armed men during the fighting. Today, where we are, we use shops and residential houses as classrooms, and some classes are held under trees. And now we are already being threatened with eviction."

a4359.speaker: "Alafia 2025" vision document (designed by a multidisciplinary team of national consultants with the participation of Beninese communities)
a4359.name: "Alafia 2025" vision document (designed by a multidisciplinary team of national consultants with the participation of Beninese communities)
a4359.speech: Presents the wishes of Beninese people over a twenty-five year period and provides for making Benin "a leading country, well governed, united and at peace, with a prosperous and competitive economy, of cultural influence and social well-being."

a4381.speaker: Djanabou Mahondé, UNICEF Resident Representative in Benin
a4381.name: Djanabou Mahondé
a4381.title: UNICEF Resident Representative in Benin
a4381.speech: Said the caravan provided an opportunity to raise awareness, engage and mobilise the population around routine vaccination for children under five and pregnant women, and also Covid-19 vaccination for those of an age to receive it ; “Beyond vaccination, this caravan has allowed us to be reminded of all the good habits and practices that we can and must adopt on a daily basis in order to live together in good health,” she explained ; according to her, the initiative bore fruit, with around 7,000 people vaccinated and more than three million people mobilised during the awareness sessions, sporting and cultural activities and mini-concerts organised with national and local artists.

a4381.speaker: Lauren Wright, representative of the director of USAID
a4381.name: Lauren Wright
a4381.title: representative of the director of USAID
a4381.speech: Welcomed the results obtained through the caravan and urged those involved to continue in the same vein ; “This campaign illustrated a remarkable collective effort and the influential role of collaboration between the artistic and medical fields in mobilising the population in favour of vaccination,” she maintained.

a4381.speaker: Virgile Hounkpè, departmental director of Health for Borgou
a4381.name: Virgile Hounkpè
a4381.title: departmental director of Health for Borgou
a4381.speech: Said this activity comes at just the right time because, he believes, vaccination remains a necessity in the fight against epidemics ; “We must be committed to vaccination, for more results, in order to have a greater impact on our populations,” he insisted.

a4381.speaker: Sanni Bio Bayé, representative of the prefect of Borgou
a4381.name: Sanni Bio Bayé
a4381.title: representative of the prefect of Borgou
a4381.speech: Praised the efforts made by each actor in achieving the objectives ; gave assurances of the commitment of the prefecture of Parakou to support the initiatives of USAID and UNICEF for the well-being of the population.

a4412.speaker: Danny Reeves, US District Judge (Kentucky)
a4412.name: Danny Reeves
a4412.title: US District Judge (Kentucky)
a4412.speech: Struck down a rule from the Biden administration that aimed to prevent discrimination against transgender students, ruling that the rule conflicts with Title IX, the federal law prohibiting sex-based discrimination in education; agreed with six Republican-led states, finding that while Title IX allows for sex-specific bathrooms, dormitories, and other facilities, the Department of Education’s rule wrongly prohibits distinctions based on sex ; "Expanding the meaning of 'on the basis of sex' to include 'gender identity' turns Title IX on its head" ; also stated that the rule would infringe upon educators' free speech rights and religious freedoms under the First Amendment, as it would mandate the use of pronouns consistent with a student's gender identity rather than biological sex.

a4412.speaker: Reuters
a4412.name: Reuters
a4412.speech: Reported that US District Judge Danny Reeves in Kentucky struck down the Biden administration rule on Thursday.

a4412.speaker: U.S. Department of Education and Department of Justice
a4412.name: U.S. Department of Education and Department of Justice
a4412.speech: Have not yet commented on the ruling.

a4412.speaker: Jonathan Skrmetti, Tennessee Attorney General
a4412.name: Jonathan Skrmetti
a4412.title: Tennessee Attorney General
a4412.speech: In a statement, praised the decision as "a huge win ... for women and girls across America." ; "The court’s ruling is yet another repudiation of the Biden administration’s relentless push to impose a radical gender ideology through unconstitutional and illegal rulemaking."

a4454.speaker: David Cooperider (Appreciative Inquiry theorist)
a4454.name: David Cooperider (Appreciative Inquiry theorist)
a4454.speech: In his 4-D (later 5-D) model, identified the positive core as the “sun, life giving force, around which discovery, dream, design, destiny, and delivery rotated.”

a4614.speaker: Benvinda Levi, Prime Minister of Mozambique
a4614.name: Benvinda Levi
a4614.title: Prime Minister of Mozambique
a4614.speech: Noting that Mozambique's trade with other African nations had reached 7.1 billion U.S. dollars over the past five years, called on the private sector to invest in industrial development and infrastructure under the government's “Industrialize Mozambique” initiative; said the AfCFTA provides a platform for establishing strategic partnerships and boosting economic and business activities for the private sector, and noted that this market, beyond accelerating the establishment of an integrated African public-private dialogue model, also holds the potential to increase Mozambique's trade with the rest of the African continent.

a4614.speaker: AIM (Mozambican state news agency)
a4614.name: AIM (Mozambican state news agency)
a4614.speech: Cited as the source quoting Prime Minister Levi's remarks; local media reported the launch ceremony.

a4614.speaker: AfCFTA Secretariat Official (@AfCFTA, social media post)
a4614.name: AfCFTA Secretariat Official (@AfCFTA
a4614.title: social media post)
a4614.speech: “Today in Beira, Mozambique, the first shipment of goods under the AfCFTA was officially launched. The consignment, headed to Kenya, marks a major milestone in Mozambique's role within the continental free trade framework. The event was led by the Prime Minister, H.E. Maria…” (April 26, 2025)

a4735.speaker: Christian Kaunert, expert in European security, Professor at Dublin City University and the University of South Wales
a4735.name: Christian Kaunert
a4735.title: expert in European security, Professor at Dublin City University and the University of South Wales
a4735.speech: Said that “We are at a moment when the issue has become particularly difficult to manage, with the election of President Trump in the US, which was based on a platform centred on containing immigration” ; said that although there had been populist movements before, this is “the most significant challenge”, and that in destination countries populism has had a contagion effect, as seen in the Netherlands with Geert Wilders, in Italy with Matteo Salvini, in the recent German elections with the AfD and in the United Kingdom with Brexit and Nigel Farage ; said a fairly broad movement is consolidating that builds its political platform on preventing migration — “They want to keep people ‘out’” — which creates problems for the destination countries themselves because many of them depend economically on migration: “If we look at the US, for example, it is immigrants who keep a substantial part of the economy running.”

a4735.speaker: Christian Kaunert, expert in European security
a4735.name: Christian Kaunert
a4735.title: expert in European security
a4735.speech: Said the impact on transit and origin countries is equally significant because migration is essential to keeping economies running, and that “Remittances, for example, are a fundamental economic factor for the functioning and development of countries of origin” ; said that “If we add to this other political decisions taken by the US, such as the cuts to USAID, the scenario becomes even more difficult for many countries”, generating “potential economic and political disruption on all fronts – in destination, transit and origin countries”.

a4735.speaker: Christian Kaunert, expert in European security
a4735.name: Christian Kaunert
a4735.title: expert in European security
a4735.speech: Said that if security policies are judged as a political objective — keeping migrants out — “that objective is rarely achieved”, and that even in the US, where a fairly harsh approach to migrants has been adopted, “this does not necessarily prevent them from continuing to arrive. It only makes the process harder and more unpleasant for those who arrive” ; said migration will not stop because the main reason migrants come is a growing economy, so “the best way to stop migration would be to destroy the economy”, which would also reduce economic growth potential in both destination and origin countries ; said stopping migration “is not a rational answer” but a reaction to an anxious, fearful society unable to cope with social change, and that current policies may in fact aggravate that anxiety rather than relieve it.

a4735.speaker: Christian Kaunert, expert in European security
a4735.name: Christian Kaunert
a4735.title: expert in European security
a4735.speech: Said that ultimately it is civil society that can ensure the human and humanitarian side is not lost, citing Germany in 2015 where civil society welcomed migrants at train stations and treated it as a humanitarian mission ; said that most migrants are not terrorists but that the association with attacks that followed the migration wave generated anxiety, and that the entry of some terrorists into Europe had to do with the operational dimension of managing that migration — in 2015 the usual procedures of registration and security screening were not applied because of the speed of the wave, whereas in the 1990s, when Germany received many Kosovars and Bosnians, those problems did not arise because it was much better managed.

a4735.speaker: Christian Kaunert, expert in European security
a4735.name: Christian Kaunert
a4735.title: expert in European security
a4735.speech: Said that in the end migration is about people, and “there will be many good people and some bad ones, as in any society”, so what matters is having procedures so that the migrants that are needed arrive in an orderly way “without having to cross the Mediterranean or risk dying on the journey”, together with verification and registration processes ; said migration “in itself is neither good nor bad: it is a question of how to make it sustainable for society”, which requires knowing how many people are arriving so as to plan resources and ensure enough healthcare, education and housing ; cited Ireland, which historically was not a country of immigration and, after Brexit, suddenly received a large share of migration: people approached it from a humanitarian point of view and said “We are welcoming these people and all of this is a good thing”, but “although they had good intentions, they did not have good planning. And good planning is necessary to sustain good intentions in the long term.”

a4735.speaker: Christian Kaunert, expert in European security
a4735.name: Christian Kaunert
a4735.title: expert in European security
a4735.speech: Said control is mainly about being able to manage the people who enter, and that if a society understands it can take in, say, 20,000 people a year, that is not in itself a problem ; said that within the European Union there must be better management among countries, which should help each other, because when three million people flee Syria and 2.8 million stay in Germany while the remaining countries receive only 200,000 “that becomes unsustainable in the long term” ; said European countries must accept that migration will happen and plan on that premise, with solidarity mechanisms to avoid cases like Ireland, where many migrants were housed in tents or occupied school sports halls so that students could not practise sport ; said responsibility should be shared globally, including by the US, Australia and some wealthier Middle Eastern societies.

a4735.speaker: Christian Kaunert, expert in European security
a4735.name: Christian Kaunert
a4735.title: expert in European security
a4735.speech: Said the externalisation of borders “is an approach that exists, but it is not very coherent” and that what is grouped under that label is often different in practice ; cited Turkey, where the government decided in the 2015 crisis to welcome all Syrian refugees with open arms without anticipating how many there would be, was then unable to respond, generating a far-right backlash, and ended up pushing many refugees towards Europe knowing the Europeans would pay — which worked in the short term but set a precedent and created “a whole structure of incentives that turns almost into a business, of keeping migrants out, and that is the wrong incentive” ; said migration has cyclical moments, describing how flows moved from Morocco to Spain, then to Italy via Libya after Spain reinforced border controls and struck a deal with Morocco, then to Turkey after Italy made deals with Gaddafi, and then Erdogan struck a deal with the EU: “The problem does not disappear, it is simply displaced”, and externalisation “becomes a real industry”.

a4735.speaker: Christian Kaunert, expert in European security
a4735.name: Christian Kaunert
a4735.title: expert in European security
a4735.speech: Said academia is very important “because we want evidence-based policies, grounded in solid and rigorous research, not in hunches or distortions”, and that academic exchanges matter because academics can work across borders in ways other sectors sometimes cannot; said academics have a responsibility to collaborate and present ideas to policymakers, who often have to deal with a crisis quickly and do not know how, and are glad to be able to rely on good research.

a4735.speaker: Christian Kaunert, expert in European security
a4735.name: Christian Kaunert
a4735.title: expert in European security
a4735.speech: Said President Trump “has great geopolitical ambitions that go well beyond migration”, as seen with trade tariffs, and that his migration policies are driven largely by domestic motivations aimed at pleasing the electorate ; said Trump campaigned on grandiose promises “that no government in history has ever fulfilled” and that “there will be a lot of empty talk, but he will not be able to do what he wants, because that is structurally impossible” — he spoke not only of reducing the flow but of expelling most people, which he will not manage ; said at most he will reduce the number of people arriving because of the impact of his rhetoric, amplified by the media with images of ICE agents picking up children at schools, which will have an inhibiting effect and may even generate excessive fear, since the US lacks the administrative resources and the system to carry it out ; said that for universities the policy “is a disaster” and that US universities are currently being attacked on several fronts — immigration, research funding and freedom of expression.

a4735.speaker: Christian Kaunert, expert in European security
a4735.name: Christian Kaunert
a4735.title: expert in European security
a4735.speech: Said that “the world as we know it is changing” and that geopolitical divisions are reaching a magnitude he has never seen in his lifetime and that most people have not seen since the Second World War ; said policymakers must understand that they will depend heavily on having good friends and being able to collaborate with them quickly, because the coming years will bring many shocks and external events — tariffs, and potentially even war ; said “I would like some people in Washington to also understand that friends and allies are indeed important”, and that especially when a country is small “you need friends and partners to work and collaborate with”, globally but starting with neighbours and friends.

a4735.speaker: Christian Kaunert, expert in European security
a4735.name: Christian Kaunert
a4735.title: expert in European security
a4735.speech: Said there is an initial conversation about Canada eventually joining the European Union, which began with Trump’s attacks on Canada and is gaining momentum among some policymakers; said that if that happened membership would not be like France or Portugal, but that in this “race for friends and allies” opportunities may arise for more distant countries to join that circle of friendship and partnership; said that whatever the outcome with Canada, Norway or Ukraine, these questions will require a political answer and the EU may no longer be the one based on the Copenhagen criteria, under which a country has to be geographically in Europe — “I think that in the future it may become more flexible”; asked whether the EU is changing, said “I think so.”

a4954.speaker: Vice Admiral Ibok Ete Ekwe Ibas (rtd), Sole Administrator of Rivers State
a4954.name: Vice Admiral Ibok Ete Ekwe Ibas (rtd)
a4954.title: Sole Administrator of Rivers State
a4954.speech: Has advised the contractor handling the State Assembly Complex project to speed up work and deliver it as mutually agreed; insisted that part of his mandate included restoring full and effective legislative activities in the State.

a4954.speaker: Vice Admiral Ibok Ete Ekwe Ibas (rtd), Sole Administrator of Rivers State
a4954.name: Vice Admiral Ibok Ete Ekwe Ibas (rtd)
a4954.title: Sole Administrator of Rivers State
a4954.speech: Explained that in the last two days of assumption of duties he had noticed a missing pillar in the State governance structure and is determined to ensure that there is a place for effective legislative activities after six months: "I had been at the Executive arm of the State governance structure and one of the pillars that is missing for now is the legislature and for them to function effectively, they also need a place to work from." ; "And perhaps, I am yet to be sure that work is going on as expected, so that by the end of the six months, this place will be ready for those who need to use it. I think basically that is what it is." ; "They (contractor) have a schedule and they have timelines that I believe they will like to adhere to. I think the State has done its own bit by providing the necessary funds, I was briefed. So the onus is on them to make sure that they keep to the terms."

a4954.speaker: Vice Admiral Ibok Ete Ekwe Ibas (rtd), Sole Administrator of Rivers State
a4954.name: Vice Admiral Ibok Ete Ekwe Ibas (rtd)
a4954.title: Sole Administrator of Rivers State
a4954.speech: Emphasised that he was appointed in the first place to maintain law and order, which will enable the State to go back to what it is supposed to be.

a5064.speaker: Health and human rights organisations of South Africa (open letter signed by Health Justice Initiative (Fatima Hassan), African Alliance (Tian Johnson), Cancer Alliance (Salome Meyer), Public Service Accountability Monitor, Rhodes University (Jay Kruuse), SWEAT (Emily Craven), SECTION27 (Khanyisa Mapipa), Treatment Action Campaign (Sibongile Tshabalala-Madhlala))
a5064.name: Health and human rights organisations of South Africa (open letter signed by Health Justice Initiative (Fatima Hassan)
a5064.title: African Alliance (Tian Johnson), Cancer Alliance (Salome Meyer), Public Service Accountability Monitor, Rhodes University (Jay Kruuse), SWEAT (Emily Craven), SECTION27 (Khanyisa Mapipa), Treatment Action Campaign (Sibongile Tshabalala-Madhlala))
a5064.speech: “We require an urgent coordinated emergency plan and increased budget for healthcare services. Hundreds of thousands of vulnerable people in SA need you to act now. We need transparency and accountability.”; write that they wrote to the ministers' offices on 5 February 2025 and 24 February 2025 and to date have not received a response to their questions and concerns, and remain concerned that there is not enough transparency in the government's handling of this matter ; state that SA PEPFAR partners that received stop work orders, then waivers, have since received termination notices, the complete list of cancelled contracts is not known, several clinical trials have been halted or ended prematurely, and thousands of NGO and academic workers have been retrenched with key testing, counselling, prevention and treatment programmes disrupted or closed.

a5064.speaker: Health and human rights organisations of South Africa (open letter signed by Health Justice Initiative (Fatima Hassan), African Alliance (Tian Johnson), Cancer Alliance (Salome Meyer), Public Service Accountability Monitor, Rhodes University (Jay Kruuse), SWEAT (Emily Craven), SECTION27 (Khanyisa Mapipa), Treatment Action Campaign (Sibongile Tshabalala-Madhlala))
a5064.name: Health and human rights organisations of South Africa (open letter signed by Health Justice Initiative (Fatima Hassan)
a5064.title: African Alliance (Tian Johnson), Cancer Alliance (Salome Meyer), Public Service Accountability Monitor, Rhodes University (Jay Kruuse), SWEAT (Emily Craven), SECTION27 (Khanyisa Mapipa), Treatment Action Campaign (Sibongile Tshabalala-Madhlala))
a5064.speech: Demand transparency in the development of the plan to mitigate this crisis: “in the interests of procurement transparency and accountability, please, immediately, either publicly disclose the Deloitte Terms of Reference and Service Level Agreement or issue a media correction”; say that at a minimum they would expect that Deloitte/other meets with all PIs, NGOs and patient communities, issues public invitations to hearings/meetings in each province as a matter of urgency, and publishes any actuarial details that may underpin any of its recommendations; ask urgently to be told the process by which to make submissions.

a5064.speaker: Health and human rights organisations of South Africa (open letter signed by Health Justice Initiative (Fatima Hassan), African Alliance (Tian Johnson), Cancer Alliance (Salome Meyer), Public Service Accountability Monitor, Rhodes University (Jay Kruuse), SWEAT (Emily Craven), SECTION27 (Khanyisa Mapipa), Treatment Action Campaign (Sibongile Tshabalala-Madhlala))
a5064.name: Health and human rights organisations of South Africa (open letter signed by Health Justice Initiative (Fatima Hassan)
a5064.title: African Alliance (Tian Johnson), Cancer Alliance (Salome Meyer), Public Service Accountability Monitor, Rhodes University (Jay Kruuse), SWEAT (Emily Craven), SECTION27 (Khanyisa Mapipa), Treatment Action Campaign (Sibongile Tshabalala-Madhlala))
a5064.speech: Are concerned that the current discourse and planning is focused on critical ARV programmes but ignores the continuation of several specialised counselling, support, prevention and treatment services for at-risk or key populations; hope due consideration will be given for emergency support to also be directed to Thuthuzela Care Centres and to close to 90 post-violence care facilities and telephonic reporting systems such as LifeLine, all reporting funding cuts; report that in multiple provinces young children, adolescents and families are losing access to psychosocial support, educational services, child protection and SGBV support because of the US funding cuts, and that facilities specialising in caring for gender-diverse people have closed permanently ; “We do not want the Trump administrations ideological opposition to gender rights, sexual, reproductive, health rights and migrant rights to inform our domestic health policies and budget allocations - so we want to know what is the urgent plan of the NDoH and provinces, to address the requirement of a transfer letter to enrol people into government care, especially for gender diverse people?”

a5064.speaker: Health and human rights organisations of South Africa (open letter signed by Health Justice Initiative (Fatima Hassan), African Alliance (Tian Johnson), Cancer Alliance (Salome Meyer), Public Service Accountability Monitor, Rhodes University (Jay Kruuse), SWEAT (Emily Craven), SECTION27 (Khanyisa Mapipa), Treatment Action Campaign (Sibongile Tshabalala-Madhlala))
a5064.name: Health and human rights organisations of South Africa (open letter signed by Health Justice Initiative (Fatima Hassan)
a5064.title: African Alliance (Tian Johnson), Cancer Alliance (Salome Meyer), Public Service Accountability Monitor, Rhodes University (Jay Kruuse), SWEAT (Emily Craven), SECTION27 (Khanyisa Mapipa), Treatment Action Campaign (Sibongile Tshabalala-Madhlala))
a5064.speech: On funding and budgeting: note that the Budget tabled before Parliament on 12 March 2025 was silent about the funding shortfall that the PEPFAR cuts have created; ask why the health allocation did not include a PEPFAR related component and what the plan is to ensure an urgent, emergency and appropriate allocation of resources to fill the gap; ask whether the NDoH has provided the National Treasury with a breakdown of all PEPFAR funding for SA and the resulting shortfall, when the NDoH will provide a comprehensive service plan to the NT, whether affected PIs and civil society will be able to contribute to it, and when it will be made public. “All of this is something that the Executive must address, now. We wait to hear from you.”

a5064.speaker: Health Minister (Aaron Motsoaledi), South Africa
a5064.name: Health Minister (Aaron Motsoaledi)
a5064.title: South Africa
a5064.speech: Has stated at various media/other meetings that the National Department of Health is working on ways of addressing the crisis.

a5064.speaker: National Department of Health / Minister, at the Centurion meeting of 3 March 2025
a5064.name: National Department of Health / Minister
a5064.title: at the Centurion meeting of 3 March 2025
a5064.speech: Stated that while including support for PEPFAR in the “main postponed budget” (later held on 12 March 2025) was not possible due to timing constraints, financial support could be available through emergency funding and that any funding arrangement reached would be announced once the National Treasury and NDoH had agreed on the amount and the mechanism.

a5064.speaker: Media reports (including IOL)
a5064.name: Media reports (including IOL)
a5064.speech: According to media reports, the National Department of Health has reportedly contracted Deloitte to conduct an ‘assessment’, due to be completed soon.

a5064.speaker: Director-General of Health, South Africa (Circular)
a5064.name: Director-General of Health
a5064.title: South Africa (Circular)
a5064.speech: Issued one Circular dated 11 February 2025 (not yet fully implemented, and resources to implement it are insufficient).

a5165.speaker: Jelaw Ongel, County Director of the Relief and Rehabilitation Commission (RRC) in Manyo County, Upper Nile State
a5165.name: Jelaw Ongel
a5165.title: County Director of the Relief and Rehabilitation Commission (RRC) in Manyo County, Upper Nile State
a5165.speech: Said more than 70,000 people are facing severe hunger following a dire food shortage in the area which has seen an influx of displaced persons from Sudan, and that the affected population includes the host communities and returnees who fled the ongoing civil war in Sudan. “In Manyo County, we have a large number of returnees in the area who fled the war in Sudan and there are daily delegations because of the situation in Sudan.” ; “They settled with us in the county headquarters and some of them in the villages and some populations from Kordofan who settled in Kaka, Kouj, Atidway and all the areas, and currently their situation is very bad because of the famine.”

a5165.speaker: Jelaw Ongel, County Director of the Relief and Rehabilitation Commission (RRC) in Manyo County, Upper Nile State
a5165.name: Jelaw Ongel
a5165.title: County Director of the Relief and Rehabilitation Commission (RRC) in Manyo County, Upper Nile State
a5165.speech: Stated that the region faced a difficult farming season this year due to insufficient rainfall, further exacerbating the food shortage; said the area has run out of food, and they continue to receive more returnees every day, but no humanitarian assistance has been provided since August.

a5165.speaker: Jelaw Ongel, County Director of the Relief and Rehabilitation Commission (RRC) in Manyo County, Upper Nile State
a5165.name: Jelaw Ongel
a5165.title: County Director of the Relief and Rehabilitation Commission (RRC) in Manyo County, Upper Nile State
a5165.speech: Said there is a need for immediate humanitarian intervention to prevent the crisis from escalating further; added that the local population cannot withstand this any longer and the situation may lead to deaths if the humanitarian actors do not intervene; called on humanitarian agencies to intervene urgently with food supplies. “The situation in Mang County currently requires urgent intervention and rescue with food supplies, because the situation cannot be delayed any longer, so we appeal to humanitarian organizations to rescue the situation, at least to assess the situation and come quickly.”

a5187.speaker: Fernando Andela, national director of Transport and Safety (Mozambique)
a5187.name: Fernando Andela
a5187.title: national director of Transport and Safety (Mozambique)
a5187.speech: Stated that the reduction in toll rates for Class 1, which includes light vehicles, goes down from the current 40 meticais to 30 meticais ; explained that the government made the decision after in-depth assessments of the tolls charged to Class 1 users at TRAC toll booths, namely the Maputo toll booth on National Highway Number 4 (N4), and those of REVIMO, the toll booths on the Maputo Ring Road and the Dondo toll booth on National Highway Number 6 (N6) in the central province of Sofala ; “We are holding this press conference to announce the reduction in the toll fee for Class 1 users at TRAC and REVIMO toll booths, as I mentioned. We would also like to share that, here on the Maputo Ring Road, light vehicles, which are Class 1, currently pay 40 meticais, and from tomorrow [Thursday] will pay 30 meticais.”

a5187.speaker: Fernando Andela, national director of Transport and Safety (Mozambique)
a5187.name: Fernando Andela
a5187.title: national director of Transport and Safety (Mozambique)
a5187.speech: “These measures are part of the government's efforts to create conditions that will help reduce the cost of living and normalise socio-economic activity.”

a5187.speaker: Government of Mozambique
a5187.name: Government of Mozambique
a5187.speech: Has instructed the managers of the concession roads to continue to engage in dialogue with toll users, publicising the new tariffs and benefits defined, as well as “addressing the concerns raised by citizens”.

a5389.speaker: James Hecker, commander of the U.S. Air Forces, Europe and Africa (USAFE-AFAFRICA)
a5389.name: James Hecker
a5389.title: commander of the U.S. Air Forces, Europe and Africa (USAFE-AFAFRICA)
a5389.speech: says the US Air Force will carry out airstrikes against terrorist targets across Africa ; said terrorist groups like ISIS were high-value targets that threatened African nations and the US and would be targeted by the US as it did against ISIS in Somalia recently: “They are significant high-value targets that threaten African nations and threaten the United States. So we will continue to go after terrorist organisations that threaten our African partners as well as the United States.”

a5389.speaker: James Hecker, commander of the U.S. Air Forces, Europe and Africa (USAFE-AFAFRICA)
a5389.name: James Hecker
a5389.title: commander of the U.S. Air Forces, Europe and Africa (USAFE-AFAFRICA)
a5389.speech: said that the US was willing to collaborate with African air forces, not only by way of security support, but also through humanitarian assistance and disaster relief efforts.

a5389.speaker: James Hecker, commander of the U.S. Air Forces, Europe and Africa (USAFE-AFAFRICA)
a5389.name: James Hecker
a5389.title: commander of the U.S. Air Forces, Europe and Africa (USAFE-AFAFRICA)
a5389.speech: on the Boko Haram insurgency, said the US had already been supporting Nigeria: “Well, I think, as you know, the US Government has provided training and equipment to Nigeria for quite a while, so hopefully that will help them out. But what we’re looking at in this conference is not that. We’re not talking about air superiority or conflict. We’re talking about how we can help each other – African nations can help one another – and that’s what the goal of this conference is.”

a5389.speaker: Lt.-Gen. Oscar Nyoni, Zambia’s Air Force Commander
a5389.name: Lt.-Gen. Oscar Nyoni
a5389.title: Zambia’s Air Force Commander
a5389.speech: gave an insight into the symposium and how AACS member states would respond to humanitarian needs if a disaster struck; according to him, with AACS, humanitarian/disaster needs like foodstuff, logistics, supplies and aerial vehicles will be easily provided by member states contributing whatever they are able to contribute ; “Remember, we are an air force – we are air forces that have come together, and with our friends from the U.S. and all the other member-states. It becomes easier for logistics to come on board and makes it easy for the one who is in trouble to be assisted. The more the numbers, the better for us.”

a5443.speaker: A friend of the author (unnamed)
a5443.name: A friend of the author (unnamed)
a5443.speech: “hey Tony, have you checked? Brother Gary Nkombo has just been dropped as Local Government Minister by the Don H?”

a5443.speaker: Analysts
a5443.name: Analysts
a5443.speech: According to analysts, Brother Gary was no spring chicken in the ruling UPND, hence the reason his exit caused a stir within, and without the government of Zambian circles.

a5443.speaker: Gary Nkombo, dismissed Zambian Local Government Minister
a5443.name: Gary Nkombo
a5443.title: dismissed Zambian Local Government Minister
a5443.speech: Out of natural excitement borne out of a victory stupor on Camnet TV, early in 2021 after UPND recorded that massive election victory against the PF under President Lungu, Brother Gary categorically stated that he would take a shot at the presidency.

a5443.speaker: Gary Nkombo, dismissed Zambian Local Government Minister
a5443.name: Gary Nkombo
a5443.title: dismissed Zambian Local Government Minister
a5443.speech: About two months ago, during a post by-election briefing in the Eastern Province, announced that all political parties, including the one headed by President HH, need to undergo internal polls at a convention.

a5533.speaker: Notables of the Bagadadji neighbourhood and Muslim faithful, including Imam Amadou Kallé
a5533.name: Notables of the Bagadadji neighbourhood and Muslim faithful
a5533.title: including Imam Amadou Kallé
a5533.speech: According to them, this borehole comes at just the right time since it will serve to relieve the faithful during prayer hours.

a5533.speaker: Dr. Abdullah Al Mouhalim, representative of the King Salman Centre
a5533.name: Dr. Abdullah Al Mouhalim
a5533.title: representative of the King Salman Centre
a5533.speech: For Dr. Abdullah Al Mouhalim, this act is purely humanitarian and aims to improve the living conditions of the Malian people; it is also about further strengthening the fraternal ties between the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the Republic of Mali.

a5533.speaker: Dr. Mahamadou Koné, Malian Minister of Religious Affairs, Worship and Customs
a5533.name: Dr. Mahamadou Koné
a5533.title: Malian Minister of Religious Affairs, Worship and Customs
a5533.speech: Expressed all his gratitude to the Saudi authorities for their commitment and determination on Mali’s behalf in this crucial period; he said King Salman’s efforts reinforce the concrete actions carried out by the President of the Transition, Army General Assimi Goïta, to provide the Malian people with boreholes financed entirely from the national sovereignty fund.

a5533.speaker: Abdallah Saleh Saber, Ambassador of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to Mali
a5533.name: Abdallah Saleh Saber
a5533.title: Ambassador of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to Mali
a5533.speech: Said this borehole construction project is one of many programmes carried out for Mali in various sectors such as health, sanitation and above all education; he specified that these initiatives reflect the depth of the relations between the two friendly and brotherly countries.

a5533.speaker: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (official commitment statement)
a5533.name: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (official commitment statement)
a5533.speech: The Kingdom has been committed for decades “to promoting sustainable development in middle- and low-income countries and to reducing the economic gap that keeps countries under the yoke of poverty, undermines their capacity to meet the needs of vulnerable groups, and prevents their equal access to resources.”

a5533.speaker: King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre (statement)
a5533.name: King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre (statement)
a5533.speech: “Acting on behalf of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the Centre has helped to relieve the suffering of millions of people in need across the world.”

a5749.speaker: Dr Gary Chapman, American author
a5749.name: Dr Gary Chapman
a5749.title: American author
a5749.speech: His concept of the five love languages - physical touch, words of affirmation, quality time, gifts, and acts of service - can be applied to children too.

a5788.speaker: Kenyan government
a5788.name: Kenyan government
a5788.speech: Is calling on South Sudanese peace parties to prioritize peace in the country by returning to implementation of the 2018 peace agreement.

a5788.speaker: Dr. Musalia Mudavadi, Kenyan Cabinet Secretary for Foreign and Diaspora Affairs
a5788.name: Dr. Musalia Mudavadi
a5788.title: Kenyan Cabinet Secretary for Foreign and Diaspora Affairs
a5788.speech: Said the Kenyan government is “concerned with the developments in South Sudan following reports of the detention of FVP, Dr, Riek Machar on March 26.” ; Called on South Sudanese leaders to exercise utmost restraint, cease hostilities, and uphold the peace agreement as a way of putting the interest of millions of people above their own.

a5788.speaker: William Ruto, President of Kenya
a5788.name: William Ruto
a5788.title: President of Kenya
a5788.speech: Said he discussed the current security situation in South Sudan in a telephone conversation with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

a5788.speaker: Riek Machar's party (SPLM-IO)
a5788.name: Riek Machar's party (SPLM-IO)
a5788.speech: According to his party, First Vice President Dr. Riek Machar was put under “house arrest” in Juba on Wednesday.

a5788.speaker: United Nations
a5788.name: United Nations
a5788.speech: Warns that the country stands on the brink of return to civil war.

a5788.speaker: U.S. Department of State’s Bureau of Africa Affairs
a5788.name: U.S. Department of State’s Bureau of Africa Affairs
a5788.speech: Expressed concern on Thursday over the detention of Machar and called on President Salva Kiir to reverse the decision to prevent further escalation.

a5798.speaker: FAO and WFP 2025 Hunger Hotspots report
a5798.name: FAO and WFP 2025 Hunger Hotspots report
a5798.speech: In its latest report, the two agencies reclassified Namibia as a more stable and food-secure country, which saw it being removed from the 2025 World Hunger Hotspots list along with Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Zambia and Zimbabwe. “Although these countries are no longer considered hotspots for the outlook period, future climatic shifts could lead to their reclassification,” the report states. ; The report shows that acute food insecurity is likely to worsen across 13 countries and territories identified as hotspots, with Sudan, Palestine, South Sudan, Haiti and Mali being the highest of concern and requiring urgent attention; Yemen, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Myanmar and Nigeria are also classified as hotspots of very high concern, and the other identified hotspots are Burkina Faso, Chad, Somalia and the Syrian Arab Republic.

a5798.speaker: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) July/September 2024 report
a5798.name: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) July/September 2024 report
a5798.speech: Stated that about 1.2 million people, which is about 38% of Namibia’s population, were classified in IPC Phase 3 (Crisis) or above, necessitating urgent humanitarian assistance to mitigate food consumption gaps and protect livelihoods; attributed the ongoing crisis to several key factors, including climate shocks, particularly the impact of El Niño, which led to erratic rainfall and prolonged drought; highlighted deteriorating livestock conditions, with some regions such as Kunene suffering significant livestock deaths due to disease outbreaks and poor condition of pastures; and warned that national food levels are critically low, with silos holding just 15% of their total capacity as of June 2024.

a6133.speaker: Dr Thembisile Xulu, CEO of the South African National AIDS Council (SANAC)
a6133.name: Dr Thembisile Xulu
a6133.title: CEO of the South African National AIDS Council (SANAC)
a6133.speech: During last year's interview, Xulu described herself saying, "When I sit in a room, I don't necessarily regard myself as the smartest. In fact, mostly I'm not. I thrive when I manage people who are smarter than me. My job is to inspire and to drive the bus. But I need team members holding the GPS to say ‘driver, this thing is not going the right way, we need to go there or there'."

a6133.speaker: Dr Thembisile Xulu, CEO of the South African National AIDS Council (SANAC)
a6133.name: Dr Thembisile Xulu
a6133.title: CEO of the South African National AIDS Council (SANAC)
a6133.speech: Stresses that an integrated approach is key to fighting the "colliding epidemics" of our time ; "Our theme for World Aids Day this year is working together to end inequalities in Aids, TB, and Covid-19. Our tagline is - Get tested. Get vaccinated. Adhere to treatment. Essentially, it is meant to bring together all these colliding epidemics we have - HIV, TB, and Covid-19. So if you get tested; you not only know your HIV status or your TB status; you know your hypertension, your blood pressure, your cholesterol, your Covid status, and you also get vaccinated."

a6133.speaker: Dr Thembisile Xulu, CEO of the South African National AIDS Council (SANAC)
a6133.name: Dr Thembisile Xulu
a6133.title: CEO of the South African National AIDS Council (SANAC)
a6133.speech: Says that to really successfully convey their message at grassroots level - in order to really shift perceptions - collaborating with traditional leaders is key. "We need to tap into the power and the strength that traditional leaders have. Our traditional leaders are holding indabas and they're holding meetings with their communities. And if they are the ones that are constantly speaking about HIV and TB and Covid-19, people will listen." ; "I come from that life and I know how well respected the King or the chief is. In Zulu, there's a saying that if something comes from the mouth of the chief, it's golden, it's taken as the truth. So we are tapping into that."

a6133.speaker: Dr Thembisile Xulu, CEO of the South African National AIDS Council (SANAC)
a6133.name: Dr Thembisile Xulu
a6133.title: CEO of the South African National AIDS Council (SANAC)
a6133.speech: Points out that The Global Fund [The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria] will allocate $536 million to South Africa over a three-year period, starting April 2022. PEPFAR [the United States President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief] will allocate over $435 million this year alone ; "SANAC's role is to make sure that the council galvanises all the stakeholders towards the implementation of the NSP [National Strategic Plan]. We are not the ones who directly get the money. But we ensure optimal allocation, non-duplication and we measure outcomes and performance. The ‘principal recipients' of The Global Fund answer to us on a monthly basis."

a6133.speaker: Dr Thembisile Xulu, CEO of the South African National AIDS Council (SANAC)
a6133.name: Dr Thembisile Xulu
a6133.title: CEO of the South African National AIDS Council (SANAC)
a6133.speech: Says the current NSP will be extended to 2023 with "catch-up plans" across sectors, due to backlogs created by Covid-19.

a6133.speaker: Dr Thembisile Xulu, CEO of the South African National AIDS Council (SANAC)
a6133.name: Dr Thembisile Xulu
a6133.title: CEO of the South African National AIDS Council (SANAC)
a6133.speech: Responds that SANAC brings together various stakeholders in formulating HIV policy: "SANAC is a body established by cabinet to ensure that there is a multi-sectorial response to HIV and it is located in the highest office in the country - the Presidency. The goal is [getting] everyone to realise that HIV is not just a health problem. HIV requires all sectors of society. That's why the plenary of SANAC is composed of government, of civil society, of the private sector, of development partners, of labour, etcetera. For example, the mining sector is rife with TB. So the Department of Minerals and Energy sits on SANAC."

a6133.speaker: Dr Thembisile Xulu, CEO of the South African National AIDS Council (SANAC)
a6133.name: Dr Thembisile Xulu
a6133.title: CEO of the South African National AIDS Council (SANAC)
a6133.speech: Illustrates the interrelatedness of cultural norms and transmission, citing findings from a recent TB prevalence survey: "We found that men have a higher incidence of TB than women. So, men's health-seeking behaviour is very low. I probably don't have the right words for men. Men don't want to test, you know. Men still use their wives as proxies to test for HIV. They say my wife is negative, which means I'm negative. Men don't want to be on treatment. Men just don't want anything to do with health facilities. As a result, for instance, let's just say he's got Covid. It means he's coming home to his family, every day and spreading it. Maybe he's got HIV and he refuses to test. It means if he's in a rural area where polygamy is a thing, he's still spreading HIV to all his wives."

a6133.speaker: StatsSA (Statistics South Africa) findings published last month
a6133.name: StatsSA (Statistics South Africa) findings published last month
a6133.speech: Showing that 688 girls aged nine to ten years old gave birth in South Africa in 2020.

a6133.speaker: Dr Thembisile Xulu, CEO of the South African National AIDS Council (SANAC)
a6133.name: Dr Thembisile Xulu
a6133.title: CEO of the South African National AIDS Council (SANAC)
a6133.speech: "It is unacceptable, completely unacceptable. So yes, at this weekend's plenary, the Department of Basic Education presented a learner pregnancy management strategy that has been adopted by cabinet. They essentially got a whole package of services aligned to make sure that girls are strengthened in and out of schools. But the key thing is that there's no nine or ten-year-old that falls pregnant in the classroom. Research shows that our young girls are impregnated by older men. And these older men need to be held accountable by the law, which means there needs to be better collaboration." ; "And I speak really as a SANAC multi-sectoral administrator. There needs to be better collaboration around health, starting at the school. When the school is aware that there's a pregnant girl and she is underage, you know, by the time she gets to deliver, health needs to report that to the department of social development - the custodian of children - and then involve the police services, too."

a6133.speaker: Dr Thembisile Xulu, CEO of the South African National AIDS Council (SANAC)
a6133.name: Dr Thembisile Xulu
a6133.title: CEO of the South African National AIDS Council (SANAC)
a6133.speech: Says that South Africa and our NSP are significant in a regional context: "In June, we went to the United Nations high-level meeting on HIV and AIDS for Africa where each member state actually put forward their declaration towards ending HIV. And you find that there are countries that actually really rely on the voice of South Africa when it comes to issues of human rights, LGBTQ issues, or issues relating to other key populations that still find themselves being persecuted because of the laws that these countries follow." ; "So people rely on South Africa because we've got such a strong Constitution. And our NSP is very clear in terms of key populations that nobody should be left behind. For example, you'll find that men who have sex with men are not legally acceptable in many countries in Africa."

a6133.speaker: Dr Thembisile Xulu, CEO of the South African National AIDS Council (SANAC)
a6133.name: Dr Thembisile Xulu
a6133.title: CEO of the South African National AIDS Council (SANAC)
a6133.speech: "You know, on 28 October 2021, we launched a sex worker plan, which speaks to the needs of sex workers. The fact that they need to be able to access condoms. They need to be able to test, they need to be able to get treatment, and they need to be recognised as a trade, in essence." ; "The sex worker plan is a complementary document to the NSP for TB/HIV, and STI's, similar to the LGBTQI plan…"

a6133.speaker: The sex worker sector
a6133.name: The sex worker sector
a6133.speech: Actually warned SANAC that this was the last plan that was being signed without decriminalising sex work.

a6263.speaker: Simplex Chithyola Banda, Minister of Finance of Malawi
a6263.name: Simplex Chithyola Banda
a6263.title: Minister of Finance of Malawi
a6263.speech: Has strongly dismissed as false and malicious the claims circulating on social media suggesting that government plans to devalue the Malawi kwacha by 150% after the elections: “These are fabrications by disgruntled individuals bent on tarnishing government's image” ; “The so-called cabinet paper making rounds is not signed, lacks context, and is clearly a desperate attempt to mislead the public.”

a6263.speaker: Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM)
a6263.name: Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM)
a6263.speech: Recently denied any plans for devaluation.

a6263.speaker: Dr. Mafuta Mwale, Governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi
a6263.name: Dr. Mafuta Mwale
a6263.title: Governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi
a6263.speech: Stressed that the central bank's focus is not on currency devaluation but on stabilising the economy through inflation control and improved foreign exchange supply; noted that inflation has been falling for four consecutive months and highlighted government's interventions such as maize imports to cushion food prices; described the rumours as “fake news designed to sow panic” and urged Malawians to pay attention to tangible economic progress rather than fear-mongering.

a6263.speaker: Document in circulation, falsely presented as a cabinet paper dated August 2025
a6263.name: Document in circulation
a6263.title: falsely presented as a cabinet paper dated August 2025
a6263.speech: Claims that President Lazarus Chakwera intends to devalue the kwacha, increase fuel prices by 100%, retrench public service workers, and raise PAYE.

a6263.speaker: Government of Malawi
a6263.name: Government of Malawi
a6263.speech: Has dismissed all these allegations as outright lies; officials maintain that Malawi's economic recovery efforts remain on track, and that spreading baseless rumours of massive devaluation is not only irresponsible but also a direct attack on the stability of the nation's financial system.

a6263.speaker: Analysts
a6263.name: Analysts
a6263.speech: Warn that such fake news is a deliberate ploy by opposition elements to manipulate public opinion and erode trust in government.

a6273.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6273.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6273.title: President of Ghana
a6273.speech: Has urged African leaders to back the full rollout of the proposed African Monetary Fund and other regional financial institutions to help reduce the continent’s reliance on foreign borrowing and ease pressure on foreign exchange reserves; said African countries like Ghana need stronger regional alternatives to the current global financial system, which he described as structurally tilted against the continent: “Our countries need access to long-term, affordable finance, but the global financial system remains structurally unfair to Africa” ; “We must strengthen African financial institutions like the AfriExim Bank, the African Development Bank, and the proposed African Monetary Fund to offer concessional financing that reflects Africa’s realities.”

a6273.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6273.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6273.title: President of Ghana
a6273.speech: Described the current debt conditions facing many African countries as unsustainable, pointing to Ghana’s own experience in recent years; said poor decisions, especially between 2017 and 2022, had driven Ghana into a difficult debt crisis: “Ghana, like many of our peers, is still recovering from a painful debt restructuring process” ; “We saw our debt-to-GDP ratio rise sharply due to a combination of excessive borrowing and weak governance.”

a6273.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6273.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6273.title: President of Ghana
a6273.speech: Said African countries spent over US$90 billion servicing debt in 2024 alone, nearly twice what the continent receives annually in foreign aid, and more than many governments spend on health and education combined.

a6273.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6273.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6273.title: President of Ghana
a6273.speech: Said Africa must stop borrowing simply to fill budget gaps and instead direct loans toward productive investments that create jobs, expand exports and strengthen public services: “Debt must serve the people” ; “That means stronger parliamentary oversight, regular public audits, and greater transparency in how loans are used. Less than 40 per cent of African countries currently publish detailed debt reports. That must change” ; outlined three main principles for a new approach to public debt management: transparency and accountability, responsible borrowing tied to specific investments, and regional cooperation to secure better financial terms.

a6273.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6273.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6273.title: President of Ghana
a6273.speech: Announced that Ghana is moving to establish an independent fiscal council to provide real-time oversight of borrowing decisions and public spending; said the government intends to expand the mandate of the Ghana Infrastructure Investment Fund (GIIF) to help attract private capital into strategic sectors, reducing the need for risky loans.

a6273.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6273.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6273.title: President of Ghana
a6273.speech: Urged African countries to adopt a single negotiating position ahead of the 2025 G20 Summit, where debt restructuring for low- and middle-income countries is expected to feature prominently: “The debt trap is not just an African problem; it reflects deeper issues in how the global financial system works” ; “But we must also take responsibility for the way we borrow and spend. Debt must not be a sentence. It must be a tool for building better lives.”

a6310.speaker: Chinese government work report (approved 11 March 2025 at the third session of the 14th National People's Congress)
a6310.name: Chinese government work report (approved 11 March 2025 at the third session of the 14th National People's Congress)
a6310.speech: "Expanding high-level opening up to the outside world and stabilising foreign trade and foreign investment are among China's priorities. Whatever the external changes, we will persist in the practice of opening up." ; "We will promote the development of cross-border e-commerce, improve the cross-border express delivery system and strengthen the construction of our overseas warehouses." ; "We will create new growth poles such as green trade and digital trade, support regions that meet the requisite conditions in their development of new types of offshore trade, and actively develop border trade."

a6310.speaker: Chinese government work report (approved 11 March 2025 at the third session of the 14th National People's Congress)
a6310.name: Chinese government work report (approved 11 March 2025 at the third session of the 14th National People's Congress)
a6310.speech: Stressed, on foreign investment: "Pilot experiments will be carried through in order to broaden the opening of the services sector. We will encourage foreign investors to increase their reinvestment in China and to take part in upstream and downstream industrial-chain cooperation. We will effectively guarantee foreign-funded enterprises national treatment with regard to the acquisition of factors of production, the obtaining of qualifications, the setting of standards and public procurement. We will provide services to foreign-funded enterprises, speed up the launch of flagship projects and continue to develop the 'Invest in China' concept." According to the published report, all of this will allow foreign-funded enterprises to develop better.

a6381.speaker: USAID Office of the Inspector-General (report)
a6381.name: USAID Office of the Inspector-General (report)
a6381.speech: Said the Trump administration's move to gut USAID has crippled the agency's ability to conduct any proper oversight of unspent aid worth $8.2 billion in "obligated but undisbursed humanitarian assistance funds", both the halt to aid and subsequent staff cuts having effectively crippled USAID's bureau of humanitarian affairs (BHA). "Recent widespread staffing reductions across the Agency, particularly within BHA, coupled with uncertainty about the scope of foreign assistance waivers and permissible communications with implementers, has degraded USAID's ability to distribute and safeguard taxpayer-funded humanitarian assistance" ; "Specifically, USAID's existing oversight controls-albeit with previously identified shortcomings-are now largely nonoperational given these recent directives and personnel actions."

a6381.speaker: USAID Office of the Inspector-General (report)
a6381.name: USAID Office of the Inspector-General (report)
a6381.speech: Said that waivers issued by the State Department to make "life-saving humanitarian assistance" exempt from Trump's freeze on U.S. foreign aid were hampered by sweeping staff cuts and uncertainty over what kind of aid is and is not permissible; said "a lack of clarity about the scope of the humanitarian assistance waivers and the extent of permissible communications between BHA staff and its implementers" hampered USAID's capacity to disburse humanitarian assistance.

a6381.speaker: USAID Office of the Inspector-General (report)
a6381.name: USAID Office of the Inspector-General (report)
a6381.speech: Said USAID programs in certain countries require partner vetting and third-party monitoring to ensure that funds are delivered to those intended and do not go to "terrorists and their supporters", but that oversight mechanisms were crippled by the staff cuts. "This gap leaves USAID susceptible to inadvertently funding entities or salaries of individuals associated with U.S.-designated terrorist organizations."

a6381.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6381.name: Donald Trump
a6381.title: US President
a6381.speech: On January 20 ordered a freeze on most U.S. foreign aid, saying he wanted to ensure it was aligned with his "America First" policy.

a6381.speaker: Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State
a6381.name: Marco Rubio
a6381.title: U.S. Secretary of State
a6381.speech: Issued waivers for what he called "life-saving humanitarian assistance" to be exempt from the freeze.

a6381.speaker: Aid workers and U.N. staff
a6381.name: Aid workers and U.N. staff
a6381.speech: Said most of the programs remained shut.

a6381.speaker: Notice sent to USAID staff (shared with Reuters by an administration official)
a6381.name: Notice sent to USAID staff (shared with Reuters by an administration official)
a6381.speech: Most of USAID's workforce was put on administrative leave last week, with the exception of around 600 people, according to the notice.

a6381.speaker: State Department
a6381.name: State Department
a6381.speech: Did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

a6384.speaker: Ethiopian state media reports
a6384.name: Ethiopian state media reports
a6384.speech: According to state media reports, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Demeke Mekonnen has resigned from his dual role in the government; the announcement came on Friday, January 26, 2024, without giving any reasons for his decision.

a6384.speaker: Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF)
a6384.name: Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF)
a6384.speech: Accuses Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, who is from the Oromo ethnic group, of marginalizing and persecuting the Tigrayans and other ethnic minorities.

a6384.speaker: International observers
a6384.name: International observers
a6384.speech: According to international observers, the war has resulted in thousands of deaths, millions of displacements, and widespread human rights violations.

a6384.speaker: African Union, United Nations, European Union and United States
a6384.name: African Union
a6384.title: United Nations, European Union and United States
a6384.speech: Have all called for a ceasefire and a peaceful resolution of the crisis.

a6510.speaker: Josep Coll, Head of the Delegation of the European Union to Benin
a6510.name: Josep Coll
a6510.title: Head of the Delegation of the European Union to Benin
a6510.speech: Writes that the 60th anniversary of the Treaties of Rome is an opportunity not only to reaffirm the EU's attachment to the values and objectives on which the European project is founded, but also to take pragmatic and ambitious measures; that since the birth of the European Communities in 1957 Europe has known six decades of unprecedented peace, prosperity and security, and that for countries long at war European integration has been the most successful peace project in our history; that the world is going through a period of great uncertainty in which the foundations of a rules-based international order are too often called into question, but that the EU's position provides certainties: “nous sommes défenseurs de meilleures règles mondiales, de règles qui protègent les citoyens contre les abus, de règles qui élargissent les droits et augmentent les normes” (“we are defenders of better global rules, rules that protect citizens against abuse, rules that broaden rights and raise standards”); and that the European Union is and will remain a solid, cooperative and reliable partner defending multilateralism, human rights and international cooperation.

a6510.speaker: Josep Coll, Head of the Delegation of the European Union to Benin
a6510.name: Josep Coll
a6510.title: Head of the Delegation of the European Union to Benin
a6510.speech: Writes that the EU invests more in development cooperation and humanitarian aid than the rest of the world combined and is the world's leading donor of development aid: “Pour nous, ce n'est pas de la charité: c'est un investissement intelligent dans votre prospérité et stabilité et par conséquent aussi dans notre propre sécurité et prospérité” (“For us this is not charity: it is a smart investment in your prosperity and stability and therefore also in our own security and prosperity”); that EU development aid goes to some 150 countries and is increasingly focused on the world's poorest regions, the EU being the only donor in the world that provides support in all fragile or conflict-affected countries; that “un environnement international plus fragile appelle à un engagement accru, et non à un retranchement” (“a more fragile international environment calls for greater engagement, not retrenchment”), which is why the EU will continue to support the United Nations; and that in 2016 the EU allocated more than 1.5 billion euros to food aid, shelter, protection and health care for 120 million people in more than 80 countries, and will continue to promote international peace and security, multilateralism, regional integration, development cooperation and human rights and to respond to humanitarian crises.

a6582.speaker: Sékou Yaffa Sylla, Director General of the Compagnie du Développement des Mines (CDM)
a6582.name: Sékou Yaffa Sylla
a6582.title: Director General of the Compagnie du Développement des Mines (CDM)
a6582.speech: Said CDM is committed to becoming an internationally renowned company in the development of bauxite resources; that its parent company, CHICO, is a Chinese state-owned enterprise headquartered in Henan province; that CDM was registered in Conakry in May 2008 and obtained the concession for bauxite mining in the Boké region in October 2010; that its mining area on the border of Boké and Télimélé provinces covers about 490 square kilometres with reserves estimated at about 1.5 billion tonnes of gibbsite-type bauxite averaging 40.79% alumina; that production began in March 2017; that CDM employs 1,403 people, of whom 1,273 (over 90%) are Guinean; and that it exported 6.82 million tonnes of bauxite from January to August 2024, with exports expected to reach 10 million tonnes for all of 2024.

a6582.speaker: Sékou Yaffa Sylla, Director General of CDM
a6582.name: Sékou Yaffa Sylla
a6582.title: Director General of CDM
a6582.speech: Said that to minimise environmental impact CDM created an HSSE (Hygiene, Safety, Health and Environment) department of nearly 100 professionals who continuously monitor the safety, health and environment of the mines, roads and communities; that it improved production processes by using extraction machinery, reducing noise, dust and vibration; that it repairs community roads each year, carries out regular waste clean-up, waters roads with tanker trucks to cut dust in the dry season and clears waterways in the rainy season; and that it holds community awareness sessions on forest-fire prevention and biodiversity protection.

a6582.speaker: Sékou Yaffa Sylla, Director General of CDM
a6582.name: Sékou Yaffa Sylla
a6582.title: Director General of CDM
a6582.speech: Said CDM continuously improves the precision of geological techniques by optimising mining plans, reducing mining waste at the source, and has provided dedicated storage areas for mining waste laid out professionally in line with industry standards to avoid environmental pollution.

a6582.speaker: Sékou Yaffa Sylla, Director General of CDM
a6582.name: Sékou Yaffa Sylla
a6582.title: Director General of CDM
a6582.speech: Said CDM adheres to the concept of the "green mine" and integrates mine rehabilitation into full life-cycle management of mining sites; that with local environmental companies and the government it has put in place a comprehensive and scientific mine restoration plan; and that in partnership with local communities it has planted cash crops on some depleted mining sites, restoring the environment while creating jobs for local villagers.

a6582.speaker: Sékou Yaffa Sylla, Director General of CDM
a6582.name: Sékou Yaffa Sylla
a6582.title: Director General of CDM
a6582.speech: Said CDM is fully aware of the importance of fulfilling its social responsibilities: it donates 0.5% of its turnover each year to local governments as a local development fund, provides funds and material aid such as rice to community villages, draws up an annual community development plan, invests in infrastructure such as mosques, schools, markets and wells, and maintains a localisation policy under which more than 90% of employees and equipment purchases follow the principle of "Guineanisation".

a6582.speaker: Sékou Yaffa Sylla, Director General of CDM
a6582.name: Sékou Yaffa Sylla
a6582.title: Director General of CDM
a6582.speech: Said that in 2022 CDM signed local development agreements with the governments of the towns of Kawessi (Télimélé province) and Malaboya (Boké province), committing through diversified cooperation and concrete actions to strengthen infrastructure in communities surrounding the mining areas, increase access to basic services, improve employment capacity, support local business development, encourage agricultural development and environmental protection, and help manage natural disasters.

a6582.speaker: Sékou Yaffa Sylla, Director General of CDM
a6582.name: Sékou Yaffa Sylla
a6582.title: Director General of CDM
a6582.speech: Said that since operations began in 2017 CDM has donated a cumulative 2.5 million US dollars to local governments for community development, built 53 drinking-water wells, one school, 5 mosques, a poultry farm and about 350 kilometres of roads, installed about 1,350 sets of solar panels and lighting equipment, distributed about 350 tonnes of rice, organised more than 170 health, disease-prevention and safety awareness sessions benefiting about 10,000 people, and created 1,300 direct and 2,400 indirect jobs for the local population, with 90% of supplies sourced locally and ore transport and road safety entrusted to local companies.

a6582.speaker: Sékou Yaffa Sylla, Director General of CDM
a6582.name: Sékou Yaffa Sylla
a6582.title: Director General of CDM
a6582.speech: Said CDM has strictly complied with article 107 of Guinea's Mining Code by seeking reputable, qualified and competent Guinean companies, and has established good working relationships and signed contracts with many Guinean companies in transport, commercial services, road safety, fuel purchasing and the purchase of materials and equipment; noted that certain technical services and goods must still be imported from abroad, and said CDM will continue to strengthen cooperation with local companies and gradually improve its level of local procurement.

a6582.speaker: Sékou Yaffa Sylla, Director General of CDM
a6582.name: Sékou Yaffa Sylla
a6582.title: Director General of CDM
a6582.speech: Said Guinea has extremely rich mineral and natural resources and that, with the commissioning of bauxite, iron and other resource projects in recent years, he is convinced the Guinean economy will experience rapid development in the years to come.

a6582.speaker: Sékou Yaffa Sylla, Director General of CDM
a6582.name: Sékou Yaffa Sylla
a6582.title: Director General of CDM
