a6582.speech: Said his medium- and long-term objectives are, first, to properly manage the relationship between resource exploitation and environmental protection through an ecological approach to sustainable development; second, to reconcile company activities with community development by stimulating local employment and the growth of small and medium-sized enterprises; and third, to manage the relationship between the company's internal and external environment by strengthening dialogue with the government, unions and other organisations, operating in compliance with laws and regulations, and establishing good internal governance and a positive external image.

a6582.speaker: Sékou Yaffa Sylla, Director General of CDM
a6582.name: Sékou Yaffa Sylla
a6582.title: Director General of CDM
a6582.speech: Said that for the development of the mine CDM transits through the port of Dapilon on an area granted by SMB, but that the area does not match the company's future momentum because the storage capacity there is very small at 560 thousand tonnes; that out of the 5 berths the loading of the bases has not worked at all; that in recent years the company has been suffering a great deal; that access to the port is congested, with trucks sometimes parked for more than two hours; and that all of these causes pushed CDM to build its own port, between the port of Dapilon and the port of Guémé Saint-Jean.

a6582.speaker: Sékou Yaffa Sylla, Director General of CDM
a6582.name: Sékou Yaffa Sylla
a6582.title: Director General of CDM
a6582.speech: Said Guinea was the first country in sub-Saharan Africa to establish diplomatic relations with China; that in 2017 China and Guinea signed a "resources for loans" strategic cooperation framework agreement and in 2018 Guinea officially joined the "Belt and Road" initiative; that CDM was one of the first Chinese companies to invest in bauxite projects in Guinea; that projects such as Chalco, China Power Investment and Simandou have brought new momentum to Guinea's economic development; and that he is convinced the strengthening of the partnership between the two countries will establish new areas of cooperation promoting Guinea's socio-economic development and making the country stronger and more independent in Africa.

a6597.speaker: Cospas-Sarsat International Organisation (announcement at its virtual meeting of 13 June)
a6597.name: Cospas-Sarsat International Organisation (announcement at its virtual meeting of 13 June)
a6597.speech: Announced the formation of a specialised international working group on the application of artificial intelligence in satellite search and rescue systems, following the meetings of the organisation held in Abu Dhabi from 27 May to 5 June 2025.

a6597.speaker: UAE National Guard Command, represented by the National Search and Rescue Centre (working paper presented to the International Committee)
a6597.name: UAE National Guard Command
a6597.title: represented by the National Search and Rescue Centre (working paper presented to the International Committee)
a6597.speech: Presented a working paper on the basis of which the decision was taken; the UAE proposed a pioneering technical proposal aimed at integrating artificial intelligence technologies into Mission Control Centre (MCC) operations, increasing the efficiency of space-based rescue systems and improving the speed and accuracy of responses to distress calls through intelligent data processing and integration across satellite networks.

a6597.speaker: Member states of the International Cospas-Sarsat Committee
a6597.name: Member states of the International Cospas-Sarsat Committee
a6597.speech: Gave the UAE's initiative wide praise for its innovation and advanced approach, reflecting the country's readiness and leadership in supporting international efforts to modernise the technical infrastructure of the COSPAS-SARSAT system.

a6597.speaker: International Cospas-Sarsat Committee
a6597.name: International Cospas-Sarsat Committee
a6597.speech: Adopted a recommendation to form a joint working group, chaired by the UAE, to coordinate technical cooperation between member states and relevant bodies and to develop artificial intelligence tools linked to mission control centres ; praised the role of the UAE, their qualitative contribution and proactive initiatives in using modern technologies for international humanitarian rescue objectives.

a6681.speaker: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) (press statement)
a6681.name: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) (press statement)
a6681.speech: Condemns the unlawful arrest and physical assault of woman journalist Anisa Ahmed, who works for the online channel Dalbile TV, by members of the Mogadishu police. Anisa has since been released without charge.

a6681.speaker: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) and Robert F. Kennedy Human Rights (RFKHR) (joint statement)
a6681.name: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) and Robert F. Kennedy Human Rights (RFKHR) (joint statement)
a6681.speech: Strongly denounce the attempts of Premier Bank to silence Abdalle Mumin, a human rights defender and journalist.

a6681.speaker: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) (press statement)
a6681.name: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) (press statement)
a6681.speech: Condemns the harassment and brief detention of Himilo Somali TV journalist Omar Yusuf Mohamed (Omar Guux) by members of the Somali National Intelligence and Security Agency (NISA) in Mogadishu's Dharkeenley district on Monday, 18 August 2025.

a6681.speaker: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) (press statement)
a6681.name: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) (press statement)
a6681.speech: Calls on Puntland and SSC-Khaatumo (now Northeast Somalia State) to respect freedom of expression and to end intimidation tactics against journalists reporting on issues considered critical by local authorities, including those reporting security matters.

a6681.speaker: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) (press statement)
a6681.name: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) (press statement)
a6681.speech: Strongly condemns the wave of attacks targeting journalists in Mogadishu amid violent evictions and gunfight on Thursday, as the Somali national intelligence and security agency (NISA) intensified its aggressive pursuit of critical journalists.

a6681.speaker: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) (press statement)
a6681.name: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) (press statement)
a6681.speech: Strongly condemns the unlawful arrest of two journalists in Adaado town, Galmudug State, on Tuesday, 5 August 2025, following their reporting on the alleged rape and murder of an eight-year-old girl in Adaado town.

a6681.speaker: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) (press statement)
a6681.name: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) (press statement)
a6681.speech: Strongly condemns the abduction-style arrest of three journalists in Mogadishu on Sunday, 3 August 2025, by armed officers from the Turkish-trained Haramcad police unit.

a6681.speaker: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) (press statement)
a6681.name: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) (press statement)
a6681.speech: The SJS and its network of members proudly congratulate its Secretary General, Abdalle Ahmed Mumin, for receiving an Honourable Mention at the 2025 Allard Prize for International Integrity.

a6681.speaker: Somali Media Association (SOMA) (press statement)
a6681.name: Somali Media Association (SOMA) (press statement)
a6681.speech: Welcomes the recent high-level meeting between civil society leaders and the European Union Ambassador to Somalia, H.E. Karin Johansson, which focused on Somalia's National Dialogue process and the role of civil society.

a6702.speaker: Nelson Chukwudi, Chief Press Secretary to the Rivers State Governor (press statement)
a6702.name: Nelson Chukwudi
a6702.title: Chief Press Secretary to the Rivers State Governor (press statement)
a6702.speech: Said the state executive council also approved the renovation of Bonny General Hospital; renovation and upgrade of Neuropsychiatric Hospital, Rumuigbo; as well as construction of a new General Hospital at Rumuigbo in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area of the State.

a6702.speaker: Rivers State Government
a6702.name: Rivers State Government
a6702.speech: Said that it decided to complete the construction of the Zonal Hospitals in four Local Government Areas of the State in order to strengthen the secondary level healthcare service delivery to the people of the State.

a6702.speaker: Dr Adaeze Oreh, Rivers State Commissioner for Health
a6702.name: Dr Adaeze Oreh
a6702.title: Rivers State Commissioner for Health
a6702.speech: Said the approval was sequel to the memos presented by the Ministry of Health to the State Executive Council; the ministry requested the approval of the cancellation and termination of all existing contracts for those Zonal Hospitals in the State, and the re-awarding of fresh contracts that will enable completion of the projects, including the renovation of the Bonny General Hospital; there was also the request for the renovation and upgrade of the Neuro-Psychiatric Hospital and the construction of a new General Hospital at Rumuigbo ; "We are thankful to the Rivers State Executive Council that the various decisions sought and prayers that were made by the Rivers State Ministry of Health for the approval of the termination of the contracts for completion of the Zonal Hospitals at Ahoada, Bori, Degema and Omoku, and the re-award of fresh contracts for their completion were approved." ; "That the request to the State Executive Council for the approval of the award of these contracts in total summed up to N26, 350, 310, 714. 88k was approved for the completion of those Zonal Hospitals, the renovation of Bonny General Hospital and the upgrade of the Neuro-Psychiatric Hospital." ; "This also included the construction of a new General Hospital at Rumuigbo, Obio/Akpor Local Government Area, which were not among those initially awarded for renovation."

a6702.speaker: Dr Adaeze Oreh, Rivers State Commissioner for Health
a6702.name: Dr Adaeze Oreh
a6702.title: Rivers State Commissioner for Health
a6702.speech: Explained that the State Executive Council also approved that following the termination of the previously awarded contracts, fresh contracts should be awarded to new competent contractors who have such capacity to deliver on those projects; emphasised that such contractors would also be mobilized to site so that they can commence construction work on those separate projects in the health sector in order to advance healthcare delivery in the State.

a6702.speaker: Dr Roland Obed-Whyte, Permanent Secretary of the Rivers State Ministry of Special Projects
a6702.name: Dr Roland Obed-Whyte
a6702.title: Permanent Secretary of the Rivers State Ministry of Special Projects
a6702.speech: Said his ministry presented two memos that requested for the award of separate contracts, the first being a request for Council's approval for the award of contract for the reconstruction and furnishing of Rivers State House of Assembly Auditorium Complex ; "This contract has been awarded to Monier Construction Company Nigeria Limited (MCC) at the cost of N19, 566, 621, 284. 24 kobo with completion duration of 9 Months." ; "This Rivers State House of Assembly Building Complex is made up of about 34 ensuite offices, two storey building with elevator, gallery, meeting rooms and conference hall." ; "It also includes the renovation and refurbishing of other existing structures within the House of Assembly Complex. It also includes the provision of ambulances and other external works." ; explained that by the time the work on the Rivers State House of Assembly building is completed, it will turn out to be one of the very best Assembly complexes in the country.

a6702.speaker: Dr Roland Obed-Whyte, Permanent Secretary of the Rivers State Ministry of Special Projects
a6702.name: Dr Roland Obed-Whyte
a6702.title: Permanent Secretary of the Rivers State Ministry of Special Projects
a6702.speech: Said the second memo presented to the State Executive Council requested the approval of the contract for the award of the construction of the 5.75 Km long Kalaibiama-Epellema Road, with a 450 metres length of bridge and carriageway of 10.3 metres with solar lights ; "It is awarded to Monier Construction Company Nigeria Limited (MCC) at the cost N29, 035, 907, 233.76 kobo with a completion duration of 12 months." ; "Again, in these two contracts, 30 percent mobilization is to be paid as an advance payment. We believe strongly that when that road is completed, it will connect over four or five communities within that axis, and the issue of boat mishap and its attendant problems that riverine transportation faces will be a thing of the past." ; said the Governor is determined with his mantra of "Rivers First" to open up the coastal areas with what he is doing on the Trans-Kalabari Road project, adding that with this project in the Opobo axis, the people will be the greatest beneficiaries.

a6702.speaker: Engr Ine Briggs, acting Director General of Rivers State Bureau for Public Procurement (RSBOPP)
a6702.name: Engr Ine Briggs
a6702.title: acting Director General of Rivers State Bureau for Public Procurement (RSBOPP)
a6702.speech: Said due diligence has been done by the agency in scrutinising the projects and the cost efficiency, adding that after due diligence was conducted, the agency issued certificates of no objection to each of the projects ; "The consideration of all these projects approved today by the Rivers State Executive Council, the Bureau is glad to inform the general public that it has duly carried out its regulatory function in ensuring that value for money has been met, economy has been met, fitness for purpose has been met in defending the stakeholders' position in expenditure of fund from the State." ; "So, the Bureau has issued a certificate of no objection for the two projects from the Ministry of Special Projects and the projects for the Ministry of Health." ; "The Bureau wants to assure the public that it will carry out its oversight functions at ensuring that quality specifications as enshrined in the approvals, would be met, and the people will feel their government, and that is our assurance as a regulatory body."

a7079.speaker: Rudolph Haingura, local resident
a7079.name: Rudolph Haingura
a7079.title: local resident
a7079.speech: Said during a stakeholder engagement with the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Natural Resources that communities neighbouring the schemes benefit minimally: “Those of us living nearby often survive on only what's left after the combine harvester has passed” ; “Instead of meaningful access to produce, we depend on leftovers. The schemes were meant to fight hunger and unemployment, but for us here, that goal still feels far away.” ; added that small-scale farmers remain trapped in poverty, unable to transition into medium-scale production because of limited market access, high input costs, scarce equipment, and a lack of training support.

a7079.speaker: Imms Nashinge, Independent Patriots for Change (IPC) parliamentary leader and committee member
a7079.name: Imms Nashinge
a7079.title: Independent Patriots for Change (IPC) parliamentary leader and committee member
a7079.speech: Echoed these frustrations during a visit to the region on Tuesday: “Thirty-five years later, we should be far ahead. The green schemes haven't evolved much in the past 15 years. The potential is there, but action has been slow and inconsistent,” citing bureaucratic delays, inflated costs, and corruption; criticised the tender-driven practice of buying fertiliser through middlemen, saying it delays operations and opens room for misconduct.

a7079.speaker: Imms Nashinge, Independent Patriots for Change (IPC) parliamentary leader and committee member
a7079.name: Imms Nashinge
a7079.title: Independent Patriots for Change (IPC) parliamentary leader and committee member
a7079.speech: Argued the schemes need to move beyond low-value crops like maize and tomatoes: “Why not ginger? Why not blueberries? High-value crops are in demand both locally and internationally” ; urged Kavango East to think beyond traditional subsistence models, pointing to tourism, agri-processing, and export markets as growth avenues: “We should package and brand our products locally, targeting not only Namibia but also markets like Dubai. We have skilled Namibians ready to contribute, yet slow consultants are holding back progress.”

a7079.speaker: Imms Nashinge, Independent Patriots for Change (IPC) parliamentary leader and committee member
a7079.name: Imms Nashinge
a7079.title: Independent Patriots for Change (IPC) parliamentary leader and committee member
a7079.speech: Raised concern about weak financial accountability during the committee's visit to Shadikongoro green scheme: “What actually comes into the bank? There's no clear tracking. Communities deserve tangible solutions and accountability.”

a7079.speaker: Vihoroka Kaapehi, Ministry of Agriculture deputy director for the north-eastern region
a7079.name: Vihoroka Kaapehi
a7079.title: Ministry of Agriculture deputy director for the north-eastern region
a7079.speech: Admitted that progress has been sluggish, with profitability remaining low since 2019: “Since 2023, the ministry has become more involved, and there have been improvements in the last two cropping seasons, but some components remain non-functional” ; said high input costs and electricity bills remain major obstacles and that the ministry is now exploring operational restructuring, integrating agri-business staff, and turning to renewable energy to cut expenses.

a7106.speaker: Kimiebi Ebienfa, spokesperson for Nigeria's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (statement)
a7106.name: Kimiebi Ebienfa
a7106.title: spokesperson for Nigeria's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (statement)
a7106.speech: Said the formal ceremony handing over four Technical Aid Corps volunteers took place in Freetown on Thursday, October 16, 2025: "The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is pleased to announce the successful deployment and formal handing over of four Nigerian Technical Aid Corps (TAC) volunteers to the Government of the Republic of Sierra Leone. The volunteers comprise two Professors, one PhD holder, and one Master's degree holder. This deployment reflects the commitment of His Excellency, President Bola Tinubu, to strengthening the bonds of fraternity and solidarity between Nigeria and her sister nations across Africa and the Caribbean. The four volunteers, carefully selected and equipped with expertise in law, medicine, and science, will be integrated into various institutions across Sierra Leone. Their mission is to support the human capital development goals of the Government and people of Sierra Leone through knowledge transfer, capacity building, and contributions to socio-economic development," ; added that Nigeria has consistently provided development assistance and volunteers to Sierra Leone and remains committed to strengthening the institutional framework of the country in all ramifications, and that the TAC Scheme, founded in 1987, continues to serve as a cornerstone of Nigeria's foreign policy, reflecting the country's sustained commitment to South-South cooperation and Pan-African ideals.

a7106.speaker: Yusuf Yakub, Director General of the Technical Aid Corps (TAC)
a7106.name: Yusuf Yakub
a7106.title: Director General of the Technical Aid Corps (TAC)
a7106.speech: Disclosed that the agency was developing a legal framework to facilitate the structured export of skilled Nigerian professionals, in a move aimed at curbing brain drain and boosting diaspora earnings ; also stated that the agency has deployed 396 volunteers to various countries over the past two years.

a7220.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President
a7220.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a7220.title: Ukrainian President
a7220.speech: “This support comes at a decisive moment, as Russia intensifies its attacks,” commented Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on the social network X, expressing his “gratitude.” He asserted that reaching peace in 2025 was a “goal shared by Ukraine and all its partners,” concluding: “Ukraine, which defends itself every day against brutal attacks, counts on its friends.”

a7220.speaker: Joe Biden, US President
a7220.name: Joe Biden
a7220.title: US President
a7220.speech: “I am proud to announce today nearly $2.5 billion in security assistance for Ukraine, as the Ukrainian people continue to defend their independence and freedom against Russian aggression,” declared Joe Biden, who will leave the White House on 20 January, in a statement ; The outgoing Democratic president states in his statement that he has exhausted the funds granted by Congress in the spring, after hard negotiations, to place orders with the defence industry for weapons for Ukraine ; He also asserts that his administration continues to send the Ukrainian army as many weapons as possible, in particular older-generation equipment taken from the reserves of the US forces ; The Pentagon has “undertaken to deliver hundreds of thousands of artillery rounds, thousands of missiles, and hundreds of armoured vehicles that will strengthen Ukrainian positions as winter begins,” he said.

a7220.speaker: US State Department (separate statement)
a7220.name: US State Department (separate statement)
a7220.speech: According to a separate statement from the US State Department, among the weapons immediately made available by the Defense Department will be drones, munitions for HIMARS multiple rocket launchers, optically guided missiles, anti-tank weapons systems, air-to-ground munitions and spare parts.

a7220.speaker: Antony Blinken, US Secretary of State
a7220.name: Antony Blinken
a7220.title: US Secretary of State
a7220.speech: “The United States and more than 50 nations will continue together to ensure that Ukraine has the capabilities it needs to defend itself against Russia’s aggression,” declared Secretary of State Antony Blinken, quoted in the statement.

a7220.speaker: Janet Yellen, US Treasury Secretary
a7220.name: Janet Yellen
a7220.title: US Treasury Secretary
a7220.speech: “We continue to do everything we can to put Ukraine in a strong position to achieve a just peace,” declared Finance Minister Janet Yellen for her part.

a7220.speaker: Rustem Umerov, Ukrainian Defence Minister
a7220.name: Rustem Umerov
a7220.title: Ukrainian Defence Minister
a7220.speech: Welcomed this new aid programme in a message published on social media on Monday, saying he was “grateful.” “The United States is a key ally of Ukraine and provides us with invaluable assistance. Together, we will win,” he continued.

a7220.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a7220.name: Donald Trump
a7220.title: US President-elect
a7220.speech: Has repeatedly criticised the amounts of American aid to Ukraine. He claimed that he could obtain a peace deal in 24 hours between Moscow and Kyiv, but without saying how, making Ukrainians fear that Washington would impose on them conditions dictated by Russia ; the future American president having promised to end the war “in 24 hours.”

a7317.speaker: Kabagambe-Kaliisa, Permanent Secretary of Uganda's Ministry of Energy
a7317.name: Kabagambe-Kaliisa
a7317.title: Permanent Secretary of Uganda's Ministry of Energy
a7317.speech: A recent statement by the Ministry of Energy Permanent Secretary was that: "the objective is to select a route that will result in the lowest unit transportation cost and constitute the most viable option for the pipeline project."

a7317.speaker: Acholi people / Acholi memorandum (Acholi Technical Working Committee on Oil & Gas)
a7317.name: Acholi people / Acholi memorandum (Acholi Technical Working Committee on Oil & Gas)
a7317.speech: In the memorandum, the Acholi fully support location of the oil refinery in Hoima and channeling of oil from Acholi to it, and fully support building of the petroleum products pipeline from Hoima to Bulooba, Kampala; they questioned the logic of why none of the key oil infrastructures, particularly the Central Processing Facility and crude oil export pipeline, are sited in their land or the North, and therefore proposed a "Trans-North Oil Export Pipeline" as the only objective, cost-effective and development-spurring option for the export of Uganda's crude.

a7317.speaker: Acholi people / Acholi memorandum to President Museveni
a7317.name: Acholi people / Acholi memorandum to President Museveni
a7317.speech: On the question of royalty, their position is that this be addressed at an Acholi-wide level on the basis of Article 178(b) of the Constitution; they also asked that people from the oil regions (Acholi and Bunyoro) be appointed to the national oil bodies.

a7317.speaker: Prof. Morris Ogenga-Latigo, chairman of the Acholi Technical Working Committee on Oil & Gas and former Leader of Opposition in the 8th Parliament
a7317.name: Prof. Morris Ogenga-Latigo
a7317.title: chairman of the Acholi Technical Working Committee on Oil & Gas and former Leader of Opposition in the 8th Parliament
a7317.speech: "We don't understand why government did not consider the 'sense of belonging and sharing' that a single Acholi appointment would have brought to our people. The reason cannot be lack of qualified Acholi to be appointed." ; "We assure him that waiting for 16 months for him to respond is not coercion but respect." ; "As true leaders of our people, we shall not fear to speak the truth and to demand for what our people rightly deserve. Any adverse consequence is a worthy sacrifice to endure."

a7386.speaker: Official toll (new official figures)
a7386.name: Official toll (new official figures)
a7386.speech: A new official toll puts the number of dead in the attack on the UN refugee base at Bor at 48, grimmer than the roughly twenty dead reported on Thursday evening.

a7386.speaker: UN official (anonymous)
a7386.name: UN official (anonymous)
a7386.speech: Said the camp holds 5,000 civilian refugees.

a7386.speaker: Toby Lanzer, head of the humanitarian aid programme for the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS)
a7386.name: Toby Lanzer
a7386.title: head of the humanitarian aid programme for the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS)
a7386.speech: Said he was "appalled by the attack by armed young men on civilian refugees" at this UNMISS base in Bor, capital of the oil-producing state of Jonglei.
